77259.q: Which piece of furniture do these pictures make together?
77259.e: A mirror and a cupboard together make mirror cabinet. It often hangs in the bathroom above the washbasin.
77259.m: The mirror cabinet usually hangs in the bathroom.

77260.q: Which object do these pictures mean?
77260.e: Laundry and a basket together make laundry basket. In it you collect dirty or freshly washed clothes.
77260.m: You collect the laundry in the laundry basket.

77261.e: Ice and a cube together make ice cube. In the freezer water freezes in small moulds into ice cubes.

77262.q: Which job do these three pictures mean?
77262.e: Fire, a shield for fighting off danger and a woman make firefighter. The fire brigade puts out fires and helps at accidents.
77262.m: The fire brigade puts out fires and rescues people.

77263.q: Which job do these pictures mean?
77263.e: A horse (its hoof) and a hammer (for forging) go together: the farrier fits horseshoes and shoes the horses' hooves.
77263.m: The farrier shoes the horses' hooves.

77264.q: Which job goes with these pictures?
77264.e: Books and a shop together make bookseller. She sells books and gives customers advice.
77264.m: The bookseller sells books in a bookshop.

77265.q: Which job do these pictures mean?
77265.e: Chimneys (a factory with chimneys) and a broom for sweeping make chimney sweep. He cleans chimneys and heating systems.
77265.m: The chimney sweep cleans chimneys and is thought to bring good luck.

77266.q: Which job do these pictures make?
77266.e: Gold and a hammer (for forging, which a smith does) together make goldsmith. He makes jewellery out of gold and silver.
77266.m: The goldsmith makes jewellery from precious metals.

77267.q: Which job goes with these pictures?
77267.e: A watch and a tool (for making) together make watchmaker. Watchmaking has a long tradition in Switzerland, for example in the Jura.
77267.m: Swiss watchmakers are famous all over the world.

77268.q: Which job do these pictures mean?
77268.e: A window and a sponge (for cleaning) together make window cleaner. He cleans windows, even on tall buildings.
77268.m: The window cleaner keeps the panes clean.

77269.q: Which role do these pictures mean?
77269.e: A rescue helmet and a swimmer together make a rescue swimmer, a lifeguard. A lifeguard can rescue people from the water.
77269.m: Lifeguards help people in trouble in the water.

77270.e: Rain and a drop together make raindrop. Raindrops form in clouds from tiny droplets of water.

77271.q: Which weather event do these pictures make together?
77271.e: A cloud and something bursting (a broken heart) make cloudburst. That is what a very heavy, sudden downpour is called.
77271.m: In a cloudburst it suddenly rains very heavily.

77274.q: Which weather word do these pictures mean?
77274.e: Heat (a sweating face) and a wave together make heatwave. That is what several very hot days in a row are called.
77274.m: A heatwave brings several very hot days.

77275.q: Which weather event do these pictures make together?
77275.e: Snow and a storm (a whirlwind) together make snowstorm. Strong wind blows lots of snow through the air.
77275.m: In a snowstorm you can hardly see anything.

77276.e: The sun and an arrow pointing up together make sunrise. In the morning the sun rises in the east.
77276.m: The sun rises in the east.

77277.q: Which weather situation do these pictures make together?
77277.e: Fog and the sea together make sea of fog. From a mountain the fog in the valley looks like a sea; people in the Swiss Plateau know this well.
77277.m: The sun often shines above the sea of fog.

77278.q: Which sport do these pictures make together?
77278.e: High (an arrow pointing up) and jump (a kangaroo) together make high jump. You jump over a bar without knocking it down.
77278.m: In the high jump you jump over a bar.

77279.q: Which winter sport do these pictures mean?
77279.e: Skis and a jump (the kangaroo jumps) together make ski jumping. Ski jumpers fly a long way through the air from a ramp.
77279.m: In ski jumping you fly off a ramp.

77280.e: A spring (a kangaroo) and a board (wood) together make springboard. From the springy board you jump into the water or over apparatus in gymnastics.
77280.m: From the springboard you jump into the pool.

77281.e: A goal (a target) and a line (a ruler) together make the finishing line. Whoever crosses it first wins the race.
77281.m: Whoever crosses the finishing line first wins.

77283.q: Which piece of sports equipment do these pictures mean?
77283.e: Racing (a racing car) and a bike together make racing bike. It is light and has narrow tyres for high speed.
77283.m: A racing bike is light and fast.

77284.q: Which sport do these pictures make together?
77284.e: Water and skis together make water skiing. A boat pulls you across the water.
77284.m: In water skiing a boat pulls the skier across the water.

77287.q: Which morning snack do these pictures make together?
77287.e: Honey and bread together make bread and honey. It is a slice of bread spread with honey.
77287.m: Bread and honey is sweet and quick to make.

77289.q: Which dish do these pictures mean?
77289.e: A pan and a cake together make pancake. It is made from flour, eggs and milk and cooked in a pan.
77289.m: Pancakes are cooked in a pan.

77291.e: Earth and a nut go together: the peanut, also called groundnut. The fruits of the peanut plant ripen under the ground.

77292.q: Which cooking ingredient do these pictures mean?
77292.e: A coconut and milk together make coconut milk. It is made from the grated flesh of the coconut and is used, for example, in curries.
77292.m: Coconut milk is made from coconuts.

77293.q: Which pastry do these pictures mean?
77293.e: An apple and a swirl (Strudel means swirl in German) together make apple strudel. The thin pastry is filled with apples and rolled up.
77293.m: Apple strudel is a rolled pastry with apples.

77295.q: Which building do these pictures mean?
77295.e: A horse and a hut (a stable) together make horse stable. The horses have their stalls there.
77295.m: The horses live in the stable.

77296.q: Which building do these pictures mean?
77296.e: High (an arrow pointing up) and a house together make high-rise. A high-rise building has very many floors.
77296.m: A high-rise has very many floors.

77299.q: Which structure do these pictures make together?
77299.e: A town and a wall (bricks) together make city wall. Many medieval towns, such as Murten, still have a city wall.
77299.m: Murten still has a well-preserved city wall.

77300.e: A church and a bell together make church bell. It hangs in the church tower and rings at certain times.
77300.m: The church bell rings in the church tower.

77301.q: Which structure do these pictures make together?
77301.e: Ice and a stadium together make ice stadium. Ice hockey matches, for example, take place there.
77301.m: Ice hockey is played in the ice stadium.

77302.q: Which structure do these pictures mean?
77302.e: A bell and a tower together make bell tower. The bells hang in it so that their ringing can be heard far away.
77302.m: The bells hang in the bell tower.

77304.q: Which bone do these pictures make?
77304.e: The knee on the leg and a disc together make kneecap. The kneecap is a flat bone at the front of the knee.
77304.m: The kneecap protects the knee joint.

77305.q: Which part of the ear do these pictures mean?
77305.e: A drum and a skin (a sheep's fleece) go together: the eardrum vibrates like the skin of a drum when sound hits it.
77305.m: The eardrum vibrates like a drum when sound hits it.

77307.e: The sun and burning (fire) together make sunburn. Too much sun reddens and burns the skin.

77309.q: Which part of the body do these pictures make?
77309.e: A nose and a hole go together: the nostrils. You breathe air in through your nostrils.
77309.m: You breathe in through your nostrils.

77311.q: Which term from physics do these pictures make?
77311.e: A magnet and a field together make magnetic field. A magnetic field is the area in which a magnet has an effect.
77311.m: The Earth has its own magnetic field.

77312.q: Which event do these pictures mean?
77312.e: The moon and a landing together make moon landing. The first crewed moon landing succeeded in 1969 with Apollo 11.
77312.m: The first moon landing took place in 1969.

77313.q: Which event in the sky do these pictures make together?
77313.e: The sun and the dark moon together make solar eclipse. The moon moves in front of the sun and darkens it.
77313.m: In a solar eclipse the moon is in front of the sun.

77314.q: Which term from astronomy do these pictures make?
77314.e: Milk and a road (a way) together make Milky Way. That is the name of our galaxy, which looks like a milky band in the night sky.
77314.m: Our solar system lies in the Milky Way.

77315.q: Which trace do these pictures mean?
77315.e: A finger and a print (a printer) together make fingerprint. Every person has a unique pattern on their fingertips.

77316.q: Which unit from astronomy do these pictures make?
77316.e: Light and a year together make light year. A light year is the distance light travels in one year, so it is a distance and not a time.
77316.m: A light year measures a distance.

77317.q: Which natural event do these pictures make together?
77317.e: The Earth and quaking (a vibrating phone) together make earthquake. The ground shakes and sways.
77317.m: In an earthquake the ground shakes.

77318.q: Which term from physics do these pictures make?
77318.e: Water and steam (a steam locomotive) together make water vapour. At sea level water boils at 100 degrees Celsius and turns into steam.
77318.m: Boiling water turns into water vapour.

77319.q: Which term from astronomy do these pictures mean?
77319.e: A star and a picture go together: a constellation is a group of stars that you join up into a picture, like Orion or the Great Bear.
77319.m: Orion is a well-known constellation in the winter sky.

77320.q: Which game do these pictures mean?
77320.e: Small (mini, a finger gesture) and golf (a flag in the hole) together make minigolf. You hit a ball into the hole on short courses.
77320.m: Minigolf is played on small courses.

77321.e: Falling (a falling leaf) and an umbrella go together: a parachute. It slows down a jump from an aeroplane.
77321.m: A parachute slows down your fall.

77322.e: A beach and a basket go together: the wicker beach chair. This woven seat protects you from wind and sun by the sea.
77322.m: A wicker beach chair protects you from the wind on the beach.

77323.e: A camp (a tent) and fire together make campfire. When camping, people love sitting round the campfire in the evening.
77323.m: At camp people sing songs round the campfire.

77324.q: Which object do these pictures make together?
77324.e: Sleeping and a bag together make sleeping bag. In a sleeping bag you sleep warmly in the tent.
77324.m: In a sleeping bag you stay warm at night.

77325.e: Treasure (a bag of money) and a map together make treasure map. It shows where a treasure is hidden.
77325.m: A treasure map shows the way to the treasure.

77326.q: Which racing vehicle do these pictures make?
77326.e: Soap and a box together make soapbox cart. This home-made vehicle without an engine rolls down a slope in races.
77326.m: A soapbox cart rolls downhill without an engine.

77327.q: Which fairground ride do these pictures mean?
77327.e: An eight and a track go together: rollercoasters used to be built in the shape of a figure of eight.
77327.m: The rollercoaster races up and down round bends.

77328.q: Which saying do these emojis show?
a: Let the cat out of the bag
Get out of a tight spot
77328.e: A cat, a bag and a person talking stand for “let the cat out of the bag”. It means giving away a secret.
77328.m: If you let the cat out of the bag, you give away a secret.

77329.q: Which saying do these emojis show?
a: Like a bull in a china shop
Make a mountain out of a molehill
Like a fish out of water
77329.e: An elephant and breaking crockery show “like a bull in a china shop” (in German it is an elephant). It describes someone who is very clumsy or tactless.
77329.m: Someone who behaves like a bull in a china shop is very clumsy.

77330.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
a: The early bird catches the worm
Even a blind hen finds a grain
77330.e: Hens, a sunrise and an alarm clock make “get up with the hens”. It means getting up very early in the morning.
77330.m: If you get up with the hens, you get up very early.

77331.q: Which saying do these emojis show?
a: Like a fish out of water
Like a bull in a china shop
77331.e: A fish in a dry desert shows “like a fish out of water”. That is how someone feels who is completely out of place and helpless in a situation.
77331.m: If you feel like a fish out of water, you are helpless in an unfamiliar situation.

77332.q: Which saying do these emojis show?
a: Make hay while the sun shines
77332.e: A wolf, a sheep and a coat stand for “a wolf in sheep's clothing”. It means someone who seems harmless but has bad intentions.
77332.m: A wolf in sheep's clothing seems friendly but has bad intentions.

77333.q: Which saying do these emojis show?
a: Make a mountain out of a molehill
Like a bull in a china shop
Kill two birds with one stone
Put the fox in charge of the henhouse
77333.e: The mosquito turns into an elephant: in German you “make an elephant out of a mosquito”, in English “make a mountain out of a molehill”. It means greatly exaggerating something small.
77333.m: If you make a mountain out of a molehill, you exaggerate wildly.

77334.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
a: Make the billy goat the gardener
Pull the cow off the ice
77334.e: A billy goat as a gardener among the flowers shows “make the billy goat the gardener”. You give a job to exactly the person who would do the most damage, like putting the fox in charge of the henhouse.
77334.m: If you make the billy goat the gardener, you trust the wrong person with a job.

77335.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
a: The sparrows whistle it from the rooftops
77335.e: An owl, an ancient temple and a suitcase make “carry owls to Athens”. Ancient Athens already had lots of owls; the saying means doing something pointless, like carrying coals to Newcastle.
77335.m: If you carry owls to Athens, you do something completely pointless.

77336.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
a: Pull the cow off the ice
Let the cat out of the bag
77336.e: A cow on the ice being pulled away shows “pull the cow off the ice”. It means solving a difficult problem.
77336.m: If you pull the cow off the ice, you solve a difficult problem.

77337.q: Which saying do these emojis show?
77337.e: An eye and a winking face show “turn a blind eye”. You deliberately overlook a small mistake.
77337.m: If you turn a blind eye, you let a small mistake go.

77338.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
77338.e: A nose, a face with a cold and an annoyed face stand for “have a full nose”. It means you have had enough of something, like being fed up.
77338.m: If you have a full nose, you have really had enough of something.

77339.q: Which saying do these emojis show?
a: Get out of bed on the wrong side
Stand on your own two feet
77339.e: A foot and a freezing face make “get cold feet”. It means suddenly becoming afraid of doing something you planned.
77339.m: If you get cold feet, you lose your nerve just before something.

77340.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
a: Bite your teeth out on something
77340.e: A person having a haircut, a tooth and a grim face stand for “have hair on your teeth”. It describes someone who loves an argument and will not put up with anything.
77340.m: Someone with hair on their teeth will not put up with anything.

77341.q: Which saying do these emojis show?
a: Get out of bed on the wrong side
Be barking up the wrong tree
77341.e: A bed, an arrow to the left, a foot and a grumpy face show getting up with the wrong (in German the left) foot: “get out of bed on the wrong side”. You are in a bad mood from the morning on.
77341.m: If you got out of bed on the wrong side, you are in a bad mood.

77342.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
a: Stand on your own two feet
77342.e: A hand, a foot and a tick show “have hand and foot”. It means something is well thought out and sensible.
77342.m: A plan that has hand and foot is well thought out.

77343.q: Which saying do these emojis show?
a: Bury your head in the sand
Bang your head against a brick wall
77343.e: A person, sand and a monkey not looking show “bury your head in the sand”. You do not want to see a problem and do nothing about it.
77343.m: If you bury your head in the sand, you close your eyes to a problem.

77344.q: Which saying do these emojis show?
a: Wear your heart on your sleeve
77344.e: A heart, a heavy stone and a worried face stand for “have something on your heart”. You have a request or a worry that you would like to get off your chest.
77344.m: If you have something on your heart, you want to talk about a worry.

77345.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
a: Have a lot around your ears
77345.e: An ear, a note and a brain make “write something behind your ears”. It means you should remember a lesson well.
77345.m: If you write something behind your ears, you remember a lesson well.

77346.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
a: Go as red as a tomato
77346.e: Two tomatoes and two eyes show “have tomatoes on your eyes”. It means you miss something that is actually obvious.
77346.m: If you have tomatoes on your eyes, you do not see the obvious.

77347.q: Which saying do these emojis show?
a: For an apple and an egg
77347.e: An apple and a pear on scales show “compare apples and pears” (in English often “apples and oranges”). You compare things that cannot sensibly be compared.
77347.m: If you compare apples and pears, you compare things that cannot be compared.

77348.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
77348.e: A green apple and a screwed-up face stand for “bite into the sour apple”. You do something unpleasant because it has to be done, like biting the bullet.
77348.m: If you bite into the sour apple, you do something unpleasant anyway.

77349.q: Which saying do these emojis show?
77349.e: A nut, a hammer and strength make “crack a tough nut”. You solve a difficult task.
77349.m: If you crack a tough nut, you solve a difficult task.

77350.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
77350.e: A piece of meat, a nose and a suspicious face show “smell the roast”. You sense that something is wrong, like smelling a rat.
77350.m: If you smell the roast, you sense that something is wrong.

77351.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
77351.e: Butter, a tick and a happy face stand for “everything is in butter”. It means everything is fine.
77351.m: If everything is in butter, everything is fine.

77352.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
77352.e: A cup of coffee, a freezing face and a newspaper make “that is cold coffee”. A piece of news has long been known and is no longer exciting, like old news.
77352.m: Cold coffee is news that everyone already knows.

77353.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
a: For an apple and an egg
Want the coin and the bread roll
77353.e: An apple, an egg and a coin show “for an apple and an egg”. It means something costs very little, like getting it for a song.
77353.m: What you get for an apple and an egg is very cheap.

77354.q: Which saying do these emojis show?
a: Like a bolt from the blue
77354.e: Lightning in sunshine and an astonished face stand for “like a bolt from the blue”. Something happens completely by surprise.
77354.m: What comes like a bolt from the blue happens quite unexpectedly.

77355.q: Which saying do these emojis show?
a: Like a bolt from the blue
Take the wind out of someone's sails
77355.e: A “shh” face and a whirlwind show “the calm before the storm”. That is the tense silence before something big happens.
77355.m: The calm before the storm is a deceptive quiet before trouble.

77356.q: Which saying do these emojis show?
a: Take the wind out of someone's sails
Know which way the wind blows
Jump in at the deep end
77356.e: Wind and a sailing boat make “take the wind out of someone's sails”. You weaken someone's arguments before they can make them.
77356.m: If you take the wind out of someone's sails, you take the force out of their arguments.

77357.q: Which saying do these emojis show?
a: Leave someone standing in the rain
Out of the frying pan into the fire
77357.e: A person in the rain and a hand waving goodbye show “leave someone standing in the rain”, like leaving someone out in the cold. You leave someone alone when they need help.
77357.m: If you leave someone standing in the rain, you do not help them when they need it.

77358.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
a: Like lightning from a clear sky
77358.e: Snow, a calendar and an arrow pointing back make “yesterday’s snow”. It means something that is long over and no longer important.
77358.m: In German, “yesterday’s snow” is something nobody cares about any more.

77359.q: Which saying do these emojis show?
a: To get the cow off the ice
77359.e: Ice, a hammer and a handshake stand for “to break the ice”. You loosen up a stiff or shy atmosphere at the start.
77359.m: If you break the ice, you make the mood more relaxed.

77360.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
a: To leave someone standing in the rain
77360.e: Sun, a friendly face and a request make “to make good weather”. You try to put someone in a friendly mood.
77360.m: In German, if you “make good weather”, you want to put someone in a good mood.

77361.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
a: Out of the rain and under the gutter
To leave someone standing in the rain
Like lightning from a clear sky
77361.e: You escape the rain only to end up under the water pouring off the roof: “out of the rain and under the gutter”. You go from a bad situation into an even worse one. In English you would say “out of the frying pan into the fire”.
77361.m: Going “out of the rain and under the gutter” means ending up in an even worse situation.

77362.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
77362.e: Black, eyes and rainy weather stand for “to see black”. You expect that something will turn out badly.
77362.m: In German, if you “see black”, you expect the worst.

77363.q: Which saying do these emojis show?
77363.e: Red, an eye and an angry face make “to see red”. You suddenly become very angry.
77363.m: If you see red, you become very angry.

77364.q: Which saying do these emojis show?
77364.e: A black dot, a target and a thumbs up show “to hit the bullseye” (in German: “to hit the black”). The black is the centre of the target; you get something exactly right.
77364.m: If you hit the bullseye, you are exactly right.

77365.q: Which saying do these emojis show?
a: Not to reach a green branch
77365.e: Green, a traffic light and a thumbs up make “to give the green light”. You allow something to begin.
77365.m: If you give the green light, you allow a plan to start.

77366.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
a: To lie the blue out of the sky
To get away with a black eye
77366.e: Blue, a cloud in the sky and a lying face with a long nose show “to lie the blue out of the sky”. Someone lies without any shame.
77366.m: In German, someone who “lies the blue out of the sky” lies shamelessly.

77367.q: Which saying do these emojis show?
a: To see the world through rose-tinted glasses
To promise the blue out of the sky
77367.e: A pink blossom, glasses and the world make “to see the world through rose-tinted glasses”. You see everything too positively.
77367.m: If you look through rose-tinted glasses, everything seems too wonderful.

77368.q: Which saying do these emojis show?
77368.e: Black, white and a sheet of paper stand for “in black and white”. Something is written down and therefore certain.
77368.m: What you have in black and white is written down.

77369.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
a: To get away with a black eye
77369.e: A black eye (in German a “blue eye”) and a person running away show “to get away with a black eye”. You survive a danger with only minor damage.
77369.m: In German, if you “get away with a black eye”, you have suffered only a little damage.

77370.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
77370.e: White, a waistcoat and an angel face make “to have a white waistcoat”. You have done nothing wrong. In English you would say “to have a clean record”.
77370.m: In German, someone with a “white waistcoat” has done nothing wrong.

77371.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
a: To swat two flies with one swatter
77371.e: Two flies and a swatting hand stand for “to swat two flies with one swatter”. You reach two goals with one action. In English you would say “to kill two birds with one stone”.
77371.m: “Two flies with one swatter” means getting two things done at once.

77372.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
a: To swat two flies with one swatter
77372.e: Two left hands and a tool make “to have two left hands”. You are very clumsy at making and fixing things. In English you would say “to be all thumbs”.
77372.m: In German, someone with “two left hands” is clumsy with their hands.

77373.q: Which saying do these emojis show?
77373.e: A cloud, the number seven and a face in love show “to be on cloud seven”. You are overjoyed, often because you are in love. In English it is “cloud nine”.
77373.m: In German, someone on “cloud seven” is overjoyed.

77374.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
77374.e: The number four, eyes and a “shh” face make “under four eyes”. Two people talk privately with each other.
77374.m: A talk “under four eyes” is between just two people.

77375.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
a: To be the fifth wheel on the cart
77375.e: The number five, a straight ruler and a relaxed face stand for “to let five be even”. You do not take things too seriously and are generous.
77375.m: In German, if you “let five be even”, you are not too strict about things.

77376.q: Which saying do these emojis show?
77376.e: The number seven, a book and a lock show “a book with seven seals”. Something is completely impossible to understand.
77376.m: A book with seven seals is something you cannot understand.

77377.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
a: Like lightning from a clear sky
77377.e: Zero, a lightning bolt and a stopwatch make “in zero point nothing”. Something happens extremely fast.
77377.m: What happens “in zero point nothing” happens in a flash.

77378.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
77378.e: The number seven, a rucksack and clothes stand for “to pack your seven things”. You pack your belongings and leave.
77378.m: If you “pack your seven things”, you take everything you need and go.

77379.q: Which proverb do these emojis show?
a: The morning hour has gold in its mouth
Save in time and you will have in need
77379.e: A clock and a bag of money make “time is money”. If you waste time, you also lose something valuable.
77379.m: Time is valuable and should not be wasted.

77380.q: Which German proverb do these emojis show?
a: The morning hour has gold in its mouth
The early bird catches the worm
Speech is silver, silence is golden
77380.e: Sunrise, a gold coin and a mouth show “the morning hour has gold in its mouth”. Early in the morning people often work especially well.
77380.m: Many things go especially well early in the morning.

77381.q: Which proverb do these emojis show?
a: The early bird catches the worm
To get up with the chickens
The morning hour has gold in its mouth
Even a blind chicken finds a grain
77381.e: Sunrise, a bird and a worm stand for “the early bird catches the worm”. If you are early, you have an advantage.
77381.m: If you are early, you often have an advantage.

77382.q: Which German proverb do these emojis show?
77382.e: An hourglass and a light bulb make “when time comes, advice comes”. With a little patience, a solution will appear.
77382.m: With time, you often find a solution.

77383.q: Which German proverb do these emojis show?
a: The early bird catches the worm
77383.e: A running person and a slow snail show the contrast between hurry and leisure: “hurry with leisure”. If you rush too much, you make mistakes. In English you might say “more haste, less speed”.
77383.m: Even when you are in a hurry, you should stay careful.

77384.q: Which proverb do these emojis show?
a: Rome wasn’t built in a day
77384.e: An ancient building, the number one, a calendar and a cross make “Rome wasn’t built in a day”. Great things take time.
77384.m: Great works need a lot of time and patience.

77385.q: Which proverb do these emojis show?
a: A sorrow shared is a sorrow halved
77385.e: An hourglass, a plaster and a heart show “time heals all wounds”. Over time, sadness becomes smaller.
77385.m: Over time, sadness becomes easier to bear.

77386.q: Which proverb do these emojis show?
77386.e: A chequered flag, a happy face and a thumbs up make “all’s well that ends well”. If the end turns out well, earlier problems are forgotten.
77386.m: If the ending is good, the difficulties before hardly matter.

77387.q: Which German proverb do these emojis show?
77387.e: Books for studying, a strong arm and a trophy stand for “no diligence, no prize”. Success only comes with effort. In English you might say “no pain, no gain”.
77387.m: Without effort there is no success.

77388.q: Which proverb do these emojis show?
a: No master has ever fallen from the sky
A trade has a golden floor
77388.e: Repeating, a piano and a medal make “practice makes perfect”. If you practise often, you become really good.
77388.m: If you practise a lot, you become very good at it.

77389.q: Which proverb do these emojis show?
a: Too many cooks spoil the broth
77389.e: Three cooks and an inedible porridge show “too many cooks spoil the broth”. When too many people have a say, the result is bad.
77389.m: When too many people decide, things often go wrong.

77390.q: Which proverb do these emojis show?
a: Don’t put off until tomorrow what you can do today
77390.e: Books, an arrow and a party make “work first, then pleasure”. First you do your duties, then comes the fun.
77390.m: Duties come first and fun comes afterwards.

77391.q: Which German proverb do these emojis show?
77391.e: A sofa, a cog and a brown rust colour stand for “whoever rests, rusts”. If you do not move or practise, you lose your skills.
77391.m: If you do not stay active, you lose your skills.

77392.q: Which proverb do these emojis show?
a: Too many cooks spoil the broth
77392.e: Many hands and a chequered flag show “many hands make light work”. When many people help, a job is soon finished.
77392.m: When many people help, the work is done quickly.

77393.q: Which German proverb do these emojis show?
a: A trade has a golden floor
Everyone is the smith of their own luck
77393.e: A hammer, a house and a gold coin make “a trade has a golden floor”. A good trade gives you a secure income.
77393.m: A skilled trade gives you a secure living.

77394.q: Which German proverb do these emojis show?
a: No master has ever fallen from the sky
77394.e: A learner, a cloud, a downward arrow and a cross stand for “no master has ever fallen from the sky”. Nobody can do something perfectly from the start.
77394.m: Nobody can do something perfectly without learning it first.

77395.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
a: Luck and glass, how easily they break
77395.e: A lucky clover in the middle of a thunderstorm shows “luck in misfortune”. Something still turns out well during a bad event.
77395.m: You have “luck in misfortune” if you get off lightly after a mishap.

77396.q: Which German proverb do these emojis show?
a: Everyone is the smith of their own luck
A trade has a golden floor
77396.e: A lucky clover, a blacksmith’s hammer and a person make “everyone is the smith of their own luck”. Everyone helps to shape their own happiness.
77396.m: Everyone can help to shape their own luck.

77397.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
a: Luck and glass, how easily they break
Like an elephant in a china shop
77397.e: A breaking plate and a lucky clover stand for “broken pieces bring luck”. An old folk belief says that broken crockery brings luck.
77397.m: According to an old folk belief, broken crockery brings luck.

77398.q: Which German proverb do these emojis show?
a: Even a blind chicken finds a grain sometimes
To get up with the chickens
The early bird catches the worm
77398.e: A chicken, a monkey that sees nothing and a grain of corn make “even a blind chicken finds a grain sometimes”. Even someone who is not very skilled succeeds by chance now and then.
77398.m: Even people who know little sometimes succeed by chance.

77399.q: Which German proverb do these emojis show?
a: Luck and glass, how easily they break
People in glass houses shouldn’t throw stones
77399.e: A lucky clover and a breaking window pane show “luck and glass, how easily they break”. Luck can be over quickly.
77399.m: Luck is as fragile as glass.

77400.q: Which German proverb do these emojis show?
a: Everyone is the smith of their own luck
77400.e: A lucky clover, a strong arm and training make “luck is with the hard-working”. If you make an effort, you are lucky more often.
77400.m: If you work hard, luck often helps you too.

77401.q: Which German proverb do these emojis show?
77401.e: A present, a surprised face and a repeat sign stand for “the unexpected comes often”. Unexpected things happen more often than you think.
77401.m: The unexpected happens more often than you think.

77402.q: Which German saying is meant here?
a: Not a pig is calling me
77402.e: A pig, a lucky clover and a happy face make “to have pig”. The pig is a symbol of good luck in German-speaking countries; you have simply been lucky.
77402.m: In German, if you “have pig”, you are very lucky.

77403.q: Which proverb do these emojis show?
77403.e: A handshake and a strong arm stand for “together we are strong”. Together you can achieve more than alone.
77403.m: Together you achieve more than alone.

77404.q: Which proverb do these emojis show?
a: A sorrow shared is a sorrow halved
A joy shared is a joy doubled
77404.e: A sad face divided by two makes “a sorrow shared is a sorrow halved”. If you share your worries with friends, you feel lighter.
77404.m: Worries become smaller when you share them with others.

77405.q: Which proverb do these emojis show?
a: A joy shared is a joy doubled
A sorrow shared is a sorrow halved
77405.e: A party, times two and a beaming face show “a joy shared is a joy doubled”. Joy grows when you share it.
77405.m: Joy grows when you share it with others.

77406.q: Which German proverb do these emojis show?
a: Small gifts keep a friendship alive
Don’t look a gift horse in the mouth
77406.e: A present, a small gesture with the fingers and a handshake make “small gifts keep a friendship alive”. Little kindnesses look after a relationship.
77406.m: Little kindnesses keep a friendship alive.

77407.q: Which proverb do these emojis show?
a: Birds of a feather flock together
The sparrows whistle it from the rooftops
77407.e: Birds of the same kind together and a heart stand for “birds of a feather flock together”. Similar people often find each other.
77407.m: People with similar interests often get together.

77408.q: Which proverb do these emojis show?
a: Birds of a feather flock together
77408.e: A magnet with plus and minus shows “opposites attract”. Even very different people can get on well.
77408.m: Even very different people can be good friends.

77409.q: Which proverb do these emojis show?
77409.e: Two hands and a bar of soap make “one hand washes the other”. People help each other.
77409.m: If you help others, you often get help back.

77410.q: Which German saying is meant here?
a: To be one heart and one soul
To have something on your heart
To wear your heart on your tongue
77410.e: A heart, the number one and a hug stand for “to be one heart and one soul”. Two people understand each other very well.
77410.m: People who are “one heart and one soul” get on brilliantly.

77411.q: Which Swiss saying do these emojis show?
a: Now there is enough hay down
Not to have the same hay in the loft
To make a fist in your pocket
77411.e: Hay, a downward arrow and a stop hand make “now there is enough hay down” (in dialect: “Jetzt isch gnueg Heu dunde”). It means “that’s enough now”.
77411.m: With “now there is enough hay down”, Swiss people say that enough is enough.

77412.q: Which Swiss saying do these emojis show?
a: Not to have the same hay in the loft
Now there is enough hay down
To want the five-cent coin and the bread roll
77412.e: Hay, a barn with a hayloft and two people shaking their heads show “not to have the same hay in the loft”. Two people have completely different opinions.
77412.m: People who do not have “the same hay in the loft” think very differently.

77413.q: Which Swiss saying do these emojis show?
a: Now there is enough hay down
To stand there with sawn-off trousers
77413.e: A “Schleck” is a sweet; the lollipop, the cross and the exhausted face show “that is no sweet”. Something is hard work and difficult.
77413.m: Something that is “no sweet” is hard and difficult.

77414.q: Which Swiss saying do these emojis show?
a: To stand there with sawn-off trousers
To have an ink blot in your best exercise book
77414.e: Trousers, a saw and a desperate face make “to stand there with sawn-off trousers”. You are left as the loser and look foolish.
77414.m: Someone standing there “with sawn-off trousers” has lost and looks foolish.

77415.q: Which Swiss saying do these emojis show?
a: To stand there with sawn-off trousers
77415.e: A pair of shoes, a person next to them and a question mark show “to stand beside your shoes”. You are confused, wrong or do not feel well.
77415.m: Someone who “stands beside their shoes” is muddled or wrong.

77416.q: Which Swiss saying do these emojis show?
a: To make a fist in your pocket
To let the cat out of the bag
To want the five-cent coin and the bread roll
77416.e: A fist, a bag and an annoyed face make “to make a fist in your pocket”. In Switzerland the word “Sack” also means trouser pocket; you are angry but do not show it openly.
77416.m: Someone who “makes a fist in their pocket” keeps their anger to themselves.

77417.q: Which Swiss saying do these emojis show?
a: To make a fist in your pocket
77417.e: A button, a light bulb and a happy face stand for “someone’s button opens”. You suddenly understand something.
77417.m: When “your button opens”, you finally understand something.

77418.q: Which Swiss saying do these emojis show?
a: To have an ink blot in your best exercise book
To stand there with sawn-off trousers
77418.e: A clean exercise book, a drop and a quill show an ink blot (“Tolggen” in Swiss German): “to have an ink blot in your best exercise book”. There is a stain on an otherwise good reputation.
77418.m: An ink blot in your best exercise book is a stain on an otherwise good reputation.

77419.q: Which Swiss saying do these emojis show?
a: To want the five-cent coin and the bread roll
For an apple and an egg
Now there is enough hay down
77419.e: A five-centime coin and a bread roll (“Weggli”) make “to want the five-cent coin and the bread roll”. You want to keep the money and still get the goods, so two advantages at once. In English you would say “to have your cake and eat it”.
77419.m: Someone who wants “the five-cent coin and the bread roll” wants two advantages at once.

77420.q: Which saying do these emojis show?
a: To build castles in the air
To leave the church in the village
77420.e: A castle in the clouds and a crane show “to build castles in the air”. You make plans that can never come true.
77420.m: If you build castles in the air, you dream of the impossible.

77421.q: Which saying do these emojis show?
a: To pour oil on the fire
To put your hand in the fire for someone
77421.e: An oil drum and a fire make “to pour oil on the fire”. You make an argument even worse. In English you also say “to add fuel to the fire”.
77421.m: If you pour oil on the fire, you make an argument worse.

77422.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
a: To leave the church in the village
To build castles in the air
To call the child by its name
To be on the wood path
77422.e: A church and a village stand for “to leave the church in the village”. You should not exaggerate.
77422.m: In German, if you “leave the church in the village”, you stay sensible and do not exaggerate.

77423.q: Which German saying do these emojis show?
a: To be on the wood path
To be on the right path
To leave the church in the village
77423.e: A forest, a path and a cross show “to be on the wood path”. Wood paths used to lead only into the forest to collect wood and not to any destination; you are mistaken. In English you would say “to be barking up the wrong tree”.
77423.m: In German, someone “on the wood path” is mistaken.

77630.q: Which country do these emojis show?
77630.e: Flamenco, with dancing and guitar, comes from southern Spain. The bull and the sun are also symbols of Spain.
77630.m: Flamenco comes from Andalusia in Spain.

77631.q: Which country do these emojis show?
77631.e: Tulips, lots of bicycles, cheese such as Gouda and the sea, held back by dykes, are typical of the Netherlands.
77631.m: In the Netherlands, a lot of land lies below sea level.

77632.q: Which country do these emojis show?
77632.e: Painted vases (amphorae) from ancient times, olives and thousands of islands are typical of Greece.

77633.q: Which country do these emojis show?
77633.e: The shamrock is the symbol of Ireland. Because of all the rain, the country is very green and is called the “Emerald Isle”.
77633.m: Ireland is called the “Emerald Isle” because of its green meadows.

77634.q: Which country do these emojis show?
77634.e: The guards with bearskin hats, tea, the royal family and the rainy weather are seen as typically British.
77634.m: Great Britain has a king as head of state (as of 2026).

77635.q: Which country do these emojis show?
77635.e: Iceland has active volcanoes, glaciers, hot springs and geysers. The Icelandic horse is a well-known breed of its own.
77635.m: Iceland is an island of fire and ice.

77636.q: Which country do these emojis show?
77636.e: The sauna is a firm part of Finnish culture; almost every house has one. In Rovaniemi in Lapland there is a well-known Santa Claus village, and the country has long winters and lots of forest.
77636.m: The sauna is part of Finnish culture.

77637.q: Which city do these emojis show?
77637.e: The Statue of Liberty stands in New York harbour. The city of skyscrapers has the nickname “Big Apple”.
77637.m: New York is called the “Big Apple”.

77638.q: Which city do these emojis show?
77638.e: Mount Fuji, the Shinkansen bullet train, cherry blossom and rice balls (onigiri) are typical of Japan. The capital of Japan is Tokyo.
77638.m: Tokyo is the capital of Japan.

77639.q: Which city do these emojis show?
77639.e: The croissant stands for France, and the picture for the Louvre art museum. Paris is called the “City of Love”.
77639.m: The Mona Lisa hangs in the Louvre in Paris.

77640.q: Which city do these emojis show?
77640.e: Red double-decker buses, the London Eye big wheel on the Thames and frequent rain are typical of London.
77640.m: Red double-decker buses drive around London.

77641.q: Which city do these emojis show?
77641.e: According to legend, the twins Romulus and Remus were fed by a she-wolf; Romulus founded Rome. The Trevi Fountain is a famous fountain in Rome.
77641.m: According to legend, Romulus founded the city of Rome.

77642.q: Which city do these emojis show?
77642.e: Rio de Janeiro is famous for its carnival with samba dancers, Copacabana beach and Brazil’s love of football.

77643.q: Which city do these emojis show?
77643.e: Peking duck is a famous dish, the giant panda is a symbol of China, and the Forbidden City is an old imperial palace in Beijing.
77643.m: The Forbidden City is in Beijing.

77644.q: Which city do these emojis show?
77644.e: The flat-topped Table Mountain rises above Cape Town. Nearby, African penguins live on Boulders Beach.
77644.m: Table Mountain towers above Cape Town.

77645.q: Which landmark do these emojis show?
77645.e: Theatre, music and the koala point to an opera house in Australia. The roofs of the Sydney Opera House look like billowing sails.
77645.m: The roofs of the Sydney Opera House look like sails.

77646.q: Which landmark do these emojis show?
77646.e: The Sagrada Família church in Barcelona has been under construction since 1882 and is still not completely finished (as of 2026). It was designed by Antoni Gaudí.
77646.m: The Sagrada Família in Barcelona has been under construction for over 140 years.

77647.q: Which landmark do these emojis show?
77647.e: A swan and a castle together make Neuschwanstein, which means “new swan stone”. King Ludwig II of Bavaria had the fairy-tale castle in front of the Alps built from 1869.
77647.m: King Ludwig II of Bavaria had Neuschwanstein Castle built.

77648.q: Which landmark do these emojis show?
77648.e: Big Ben is the great bell in the clock tower of the Houses of Parliament in London. People often call the whole tower Big Ben; since 2012 its official name has been the Elizabeth Tower.
77648.m: Big Ben is really the name of the great bell in London’s clock tower.

77649.q: Which landmark do these emojis show?
77649.e: Mont-Saint-Michel is an island with an abbey off the coast of France. At high tide, the rock with its abbey and walls is surrounded by the sea.
77649.m: At high tide, Mont-Saint-Michel is surrounded by the sea.

77650.q: Which landmark do these emojis show?
77650.e: A white house and the bald eagle, the national bird of the USA, stand for the White House in Washington. The President of the USA lives and works there.
77650.m: The President of the USA lives in the White House.

77651.q: Which landmark do these emojis show?
77651.e: At around 828 metres, the Burj Khalifa in Dubai is the tallest building in the world (as of 2026). The camel points to the desert on the Gulf.
77651.m: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai is the tallest building in the world (as of 2026).

77652.q: Which landmark do these emojis show?
77652.e: On top of the Brandenburg Gate in Berlin stands the Quadriga, a chariot with four horses. The bear is the heraldic animal of Berlin.
77652.m: On top of the Brandenburg Gate there is a chariot with four horses.

77653.q: Which landmark do these emojis show?
77653.e: Waffles and chocolate point to Belgium. The Atomium in Brussels has the shape of a hugely enlarged iron crystal made of spheres.

77654.q: Which speciality do these emojis show?
77654.e: Rice, raw fish and seaweed (nori), eaten with chopsticks, make sushi from Japan.
77654.m: Sushi is a Japanese speciality made of rice and fish.

77655.q: Which speciality do these emojis show?
77655.e: A fried sausage cut into slices with tomato sauce and curry powder is currywurst. It is a typical street food in Berlin.
77655.m: Currywurst is a well-known street food from Berlin.

77656.q: Which speciality do these emojis show?
77656.e: Rice with seafood, cooked in a large flat pan, is paella from Spain. It comes from the area around Valencia.
77656.m: Paella comes from Valencia in Spain.

77657.q: Which speciality do these emojis show?
77657.e: Mashed avocado with onions, lime juice and chilli makes guacamole. The dip comes from Mexico.

77658.q: Which speciality do these emojis show?
77658.e: Cucumber, garlic and yoghurt make tzatziki, a cold sauce from Greece.
77658.m: Tzatziki is a Greek yoghurt sauce with cucumber.

77659.q: Which speciality do these emojis show?
77659.e: Fried fish with chips and salt is fish and chips, a well-known dish from Great Britain.
77659.m: Fish and chips is a British dish.

77660.q: Which speciality do these emojis show?
77660.e: Grated potatoes fried golden brown in butter in a pan make rösti. It is seen as typical of German-speaking Switzerland.
77660.m: Rösti is seen as a typical dish of German-speaking Switzerland.

77661.q: Which speciality do these emojis show?
77661.e: Kaiserschmarrn is a torn-up egg pancake, often with raisins. According to a legend, it is named after Emperor Franz Joseph of Austria.
77661.m: Kaiserschmarrn is an Austrian sweet dish.

77662.q: Which speciality do these emojis show?
77662.e: Spaghetti with a tomato sauce with beef is called spaghetti bolognese. The meat sauce is named after the city of Bologna.
77662.m: Bolognese sauce is named after the city of Bologna.

77663.q: Which Swiss city do these emojis show?
77663.e: The International Olympic Committee has its headquarters in Lausanne on Lake Geneva, and there is also the Olympic Museum. Lausanne is the only Swiss city with a metro.
77663.m: Lausanne calls itself the Olympic Capital.

77664.q: Which Swiss city do these emojis show?
77664.e: The basilisk, a dragon-like mythical creature, is the heraldic animal of Basel. The Basel carnival with drums and the Rhine ferries are typical of the city.
77664.m: The basilisk is the heraldic animal of Basel.

77665.q: Which Swiss city do these emojis show?
77665.e: Two lions hold the Zurich coat of arms. Zurich is an important banking centre and lies on Lake Zurich.
77665.m: Zurich is the largest city in Switzerland.

77666.q: Which Swiss city do these emojis show?
77666.e: Below Schaffhausen, the Rhine plunges over the Rhine Falls. The round Munot fortress is the city's landmark, and a ram leaps on its coat of arms.
77666.m: The Munot fortress is the landmark of Schaffhausen.

77667.q: Which Swiss city do these emojis show?
77667.e: Locarno in sunny Ticino holds an international film festival every year. Its prize is called the “Golden Leopard” (Pardo d'oro).
77667.m: At the Locarno Film Festival you can win the Golden Leopard.

77668.q: Which Swiss city do these emojis show?
77668.e: Bellinzona, the capital of Ticino, is famous for its three castles. They are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
77668.m: The three castles of Bellinzona are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

77669.q: Which Swiss city do these emojis show?
77669.e: St Gallen is known for its Abbey Library (UNESCO World Heritage), the St Gallen bratwurst and its embroidery.
77669.m: St Gallen is famous for its embroidery.

77670.q: Which Swiss city do these emojis show?
77670.e: Biel/Bienne is the largest bilingual city in Switzerland: people speak German and French. Biel is also an important centre of the watch industry.
77670.m: Biel is the largest bilingual city in Switzerland.

77671.q: Which Swiss city do these emojis show?
77671.e: Solothurn is the city of the number 11: it was the 11th canton to join the Confederation, and St Ursus Cathedral has, for example, 11 bells and 11 altars.
77671.m: The number 11 is Solothurn's lucky number.

77672.q: Which canton do these emojis mean?
77672.e: The Uri bull is the heraldic animal of Uri. According to legend, William Tell, who is said to have shot an apple off his son's head, came from a village in Uri.
77672.m: According to legend, William Tell came from Uri.

77673.q: Which canton do these emojis mean?
77673.e: The ibex is on the coat of arms of the Grisons. The Grisons is the only trilingual canton: German, Romansh and Italian.
77673.m: The Grisons is the only trilingual canton.

77674.q: Which canton do these emojis mean?
77674.e: Thanks to the mild climate, palm trees grow in Ticino, it is sunny, and people speak Italian.

77675.q: Which canton do these emojis mean?
77675.e: The coat of arms of Valais shows 13 stars. They stand for the former “Zenden”, the districts of the canton.
77675.m: 13 stars shine on the coat of arms of Valais.

77676.q: Which canton do these emojis mean?
77676.e: Two golden lions stand on the coat of arms of Thurgau. Because of its many apple trees, the canton is jokingly called “Mostindien” (Cider India).
77676.m: Thurgau is known for its many apple trees.

77677.q: Which canton do these emojis mean?
77677.e: The canton of Jura is the youngest canton in Switzerland. It was founded in 1979 and split off from the canton of Bern.
77677.m: Since 1979, Jura has been the youngest canton in Switzerland.

77678.q: Which canton do these emojis mean?
77678.e: The little town of Gruyères with its castle lies in the canton of Fribourg; Gruyère cheese comes from there. The canton is bilingual, French and German.
77678.m: Gruyère cheese comes from the canton of Fribourg.

77679.q: Which canton do these emojis mean?
77679.e: The Aargau coat of arms shows three white stars and a wavy river, which stands for the Aare.
77679.m: On the Aargau coat of arms you can see three stars and a river.

77680.q: Which continent do these emojis mean?
77680.e: Lions, giraffes, zebras and African elephants live in the savannah of Africa.
77680.m: Giraffes and zebras live in the wild only in Africa.

77681.q: Which continent do these emojis mean?
77681.e: The boomerang comes from the Aborigines, and kangaroos live in the wild almost only in Australia. Surfing on long beaches is very popular there.
77681.m: The boomerang is a throwing stick of the Aborigines in Australia.

77682.q: Which continent do these emojis mean?
77682.e: Antarctica at the South Pole is almost completely covered in ice. Penguins live there, and people only stay for a while in research stations.
77682.m: In Antarctica, people live only in research stations.

77683.q: Which continent do these emojis mean?
77683.e: Llamas live in the Andes, and the Amazon rainforest with many parrots lies in South America.
77683.m: The largest rainforest on Earth is in South America.

77684.q: Which continent do these emojis mean?
77684.e: Giant pandas and tigers live in Asia. Rice is a staple food there, and pagodas are typical buildings.
77684.m: Asia is the largest continent on Earth.

77685.q: Which continent do these emojis mean?
77685.e: The bison and the bald eagle live in North America. The maple leaf is the symbol of Canada.
77685.m: The bison is the largest land animal in North America.

77686.q: Which continent is named after the legendary figure in these emojis?
77686.e: According to Greek legend, Zeus, in the form of a bull, carried the princess Europa away across the sea. The continent is named after her.
77686.m: The continent of Europe is named after a princess from legend.

77687.q: Which supercontinent do these emojis mean?
77687.e: At the start of the age of the dinosaurs, all the continents fitted together like puzzle pieces to form the supercontinent Pangaea. Later it broke apart.
77687.m: About 200 million years ago, all the continents together formed Pangaea.

77688.q: Which island or group of islands do these emojis show?
77688.e: Hawaii is known for flower garlands, active volcanoes, pineapples and as the home of surfing.
77688.m: There are active volcanoes on Hawaii.

77689.q: Which island do these emojis show?
77689.e: Sicily belongs to Italy and has the volcano Etna. Lots of lemons grow on the island.
77689.m: Etna on Sicily is the highest active volcano in Europe.

77690.q: Which island do these emojis show?
77690.e: Greenland is the largest island in the world and is mostly covered in ice. Polar bears live there too.
77690.m: Greenland is the largest island in the world.

77691.q: Which group of islands do these emojis show?
77691.e: Giant tortoises and marine iguanas live on the Galápagos Islands. The scientist Charles Darwin studied the animals there in 1835.
77691.m: Charles Darwin studied the animals of the Galápagos Islands.

77692.q: Which island do these emojis show?
77692.e: Easter Island is famous for its huge stone figures, the moai. Europeans reached it on Easter Sunday in 1722, hence the name.
77692.m: Easter Island was reached by Europeans on an Easter Sunday.

77693.q: Which island do these emojis show?
77693.e: Most people on the Indonesian island of Bali are Hindus; there are many temples, rice terraces and a well-known monkey forest.
77693.m: There are thousands of Hindu temples on Bali.

77694.q: Which island country do these emojis mean?
77694.e: Sri Lanka is famous for its tea (Ceylon tea) and has wild Asian elephants. Cricket is the most popular sport there.
77694.m: Ceylon tea comes from Sri Lanka.

77695.q: Which island do these emojis show?
77695.e: Mainau in Lake Constance is called the “Flower Island”. It has large gardens and a butterfly house.
77695.m: Mainau in Lake Constance is a flower island.

77696.q: Which river do these emojis mean?
77696.e: The Yangtze is the longest river in China and in Asia. On it stands the Three Gorges Dam with one of the largest hydroelectric power stations in the world.
77696.m: The Yangtze is the longest river in Asia.

77697.q: Which river do these emojis mean?
77697.e: The Amazon flows through the largest rainforest on Earth. No other river carries so much water.
77697.m: The Amazon carries more water than any other river.

77698.q: Which river do these emojis mean?
77698.e: According to legend, a beautiful woman on the Lorelei rock by the Rhine distracted boatmen with her singing. The Rhine is an important shipping route.
77698.m: The Lorelei rock stands by the Rhine.

77699.q: Which river do these emojis mean?
77699.e: Johann Strauss (the Younger) composed the famous waltz “The Blue Danube”.
77699.m: The waltz “The Blue Danube” is by Johann Strauss (the Younger).

77700.q: Which river do these emojis mean?
77700.e: The Thames flows through London. Every year the famous Boat Race between Oxford and Cambridge takes place on it.

77701.q: Which river do these emojis mean?
77701.e: The Seine flows through Paris. Lots of tourist boats sail along it past the sights.

77702.q: Which river do these emojis mean?
77702.e: Paddle steamers travelled on the Mississippi; near its mouth lies New Orleans, the home of jazz. Alligators live in its swamps.
77702.m: New Orleans lies near the mouth of the Mississippi.

77703.q: Which river do these emojis mean?
77703.e: In Bern, lots of people float down the Aare in summer. The Aare is the longest river that flows entirely within Switzerland.
77703.m: The Aare is the longest river entirely within Switzerland.

77704.q: Which mountain range do these emojis mean?
77704.e: The Himalayas are the highest mountain range on Earth. Mount Everest, at about 8849 metres, stands there and is the goal of many climbers.
77704.m: The Himalayas are the highest mountain range on Earth.

77705.q: Which mountain range do these emojis mean?
77705.e: At about 7000 kilometres, the Andes in South America are the longest mountain range above sea level. Llamas live there.
77705.m: The Andes are the longest mountain range on land.

77706.q: Which mountain range do these emojis mean?
77706.e: The Rocky Mountains in western North America are home to grizzly bears. Cowboys stand for the Wild West of the USA.
77706.m: The Rocky Mountains lie in western North America.

77707.q: Which mountain range do these emojis mean?
77707.e: The Pyrenees form the border between France (croissant) and Spain (flamenco).
77707.m: The Pyrenees separate France and Spain.

77708.q: Which mountain range do these emojis mean?
77708.e: The Jurassic period of the dinosaurs is named after the Jura mountains. The Jura arc is home to the watch industry.
77708.m: The Jurassic period is named after the Jura mountains.

77709.q: Which mountain range do these emojis mean?
77709.e: In Greek legend, the Titan Atlas holds up the sky. The Atlas Mountains in North Africa, which border the Sahara, are named after him.
77709.m: The Atlas Mountains lie in North Africa.

77710.q: Which mountain range do these emojis mean?
77710.e: The fictional Count Dracula lives in a castle in Transylvania. This region of Romania is surrounded by the Carpathians.
77710.m: Transylvania in Romania lies in the Carpathians.

77711.q: Which mountain range do these emojis mean?
77711.e: Black and forest make Black Forest. These low mountains in southern Germany are known for Black Forest gateau.
77711.m: The Black Forest is a low mountain range in southern Germany.

77712.q: Which desert do these emojis mean?
77712.e: The Sahara in North Africa is the largest hot desert on Earth. Camels have long been important pack animals there.
77712.m: The Sahara is the largest hot desert on Earth.

77713.q: Which desert do these emojis mean?
77713.e: Bactrian camels with two humps live in the Gobi in Asia. Many dinosaur fossils have been found there, and the winters are freezing cold.
77713.m: Many dinosaur fossils have been found in the Gobi Desert.

77714.q: Which desert do these emojis mean?
77714.e: It almost never rains in the Atacama in Chile; it is seen as the driest desert outside the polar regions. Because of the clear sky, there are large observatories there.
77714.m: The Atacama is one of the driest deserts on Earth.

77715.q: Which desert do these emojis mean?
77715.e: The Namib reaches as far as the Atlantic and has high red dunes. It is seen as the oldest desert on Earth.
77715.m: The Namib is seen as the oldest desert on Earth.

77716.q: Which desert valley do these emojis mean?
77716.e: In Death Valley in 1913, 56.7 degrees was measured, the highest officially recognised air temperature on Earth.
77716.m: The highest air temperature on Earth was measured in Death Valley.

77717.q: Which word do these emojis mean?
77717.e: An oasis is a place in the desert with water, where palm trees grow. Caravans stop there.
77717.m: In an oasis there is water in the middle of the desert.

77718.q: Which word do these emojis mean?
77718.e: In great heat in the desert, you sometimes think you can see water that is not really there. This optical illusion is called a mirage.
77718.m: A mirage is an optical illusion caused by the air.

77719.q: Which word do these emojis mean?
77719.e: Wind and sand (as in the hourglass) make a hill of sand. A hill like this, piled up by the wind, is called a dune.
77719.m: Dunes are piled up by the wind.

77720.q: Which sight do these emojis show?
77720.e: In the Wild West of the USA, the Colorado River has carved a huge, deep gorge into the rock over millions of years: the Grand Canyon.
77720.m: The Colorado River carved the Grand Canyon.

77721.q: Which sight do these emojis show?
77721.e: Uluru is a huge, reddish rock in the middle of the Australian desert. It is a sacred place for the Aborigines.
77721.m: Uluru is a sacred rock of the Aborigines in Australia.

77722.q: Which sight do these emojis show?
77722.e: Niagara Falls lie on the border between Canada (maple leaf) and the USA. Huge amounts of water plunge into the depths there.
77722.m: Niagara Falls lie between Canada and the USA.

77723.q: Which sight do these emojis show?
77723.e: At the Landwasser Viaduct in the Grisons, the Rhaetian Railway crosses a high, curved stone bridge straight into a tunnel in the rock face.
77723.m: The Landwasser Viaduct leads straight into a tunnel in the rock face.

77724.q: Which sight do these emojis show?
77724.e: The Creux du Van in the Neuchâtel Jura is a huge rock basin, shaped like a bowl, with rock walls about 160 metres high. Ibex live there.
77724.m: The Creux du Van is a huge rock basin in the Jura.

77725.q: Which sight do these emojis show?
77725.e: Chillon Castle stands near Montreux right in Lake Geneva. Its dungeon is famous: the prisoner François Bonivard was chained up there.
77725.m: Chillon Castle stands in Lake Geneva near Montreux.

77726.q: Which sight do these emojis show?
77726.e: Petra in Jordan is an ancient city whose buildings were carved straight into pink rock.
77726.m: The rock city of Petra is in Jordan.

77727.q: Which sight do these emojis show?
77727.e: At Mount Rushmore in the USA, the heads of four presidents are carved huge into the rock: Washington, Jefferson, Roosevelt and Lincoln.
77727.m: Four presidents are carved into the rock at Mount Rushmore.

77728.q: Which heavenly body do these emojis mean?
77728.e: A comet is a lump of ice and dust. When it comes close to the Sun, some of the ice evaporates and a glowing tail forms.
77728.m: A comet forms a tail near the Sun.

77729.q: Which event in the sky does this order show?
77729.e: The Earth is between the Sun and the Moon. Then the Earth's shadow falls on the Moon and there is a lunar eclipse.
77729.m: In a lunar eclipse, the Earth casts its shadow on the Moon.

77730.q: Which device circles the Earth here and sends signals?
77730.e: A satellite circles the Earth and sends data by radio to aerials on the ground. Satellites provide, for example, weather pictures, TV programmes and signals for navigation.
77730.m: Satellites provide weather pictures and navigation signals.

77731.q: Which building do these pictures make?
77731.e: A building with a telescope for watching the stars is called an observatory. A planetarium, on the other hand, shows the sky as a projection on a dome.
77731.m: In an observatory, people watch the sky with large telescopes.

77732.q: Which phase of the Moon do these emojis make?
77732.e: New and moon together make new moon. Then the Moon is between the Earth and the Sun and we cannot see its lit side.
77732.m: At new moon, the Moon can hardly be seen in the sky.

77733.q: Which planet do these pictures mean?
77733.e: The red planet is Mars. It glows reddish because its ground contains lots of dust with iron in it.
77733.m: Mars is called the red planet because of its colour.

77734.q: Which planet is known for these pictures?
77734.e: Saturn is famous for its large, bright rings. They are made of countless lumps of ice and rock.
77734.m: Saturn has the most striking rings of all the planets.

77735.q: Which object in space do these emojis show?
77735.e: Black and hole make black hole. Its gravity is so strong that not even light can escape.
77735.m: Not even light can escape from a black hole.

77736.q: Which natural event do these emojis show?
77736.e: Volcano and explosion together make volcanic eruption. Molten rock, gas and ash come out from inside the Earth.
77736.m: In a volcanic eruption, material from inside the Earth reaches the surface.

77737.q: What is flowing out of the volcano here?
77737.e: Glowing rock that flows like a river is a lava flow. Lava can be over 1000 degrees hot.
77737.m: A lava flow is made of liquid, glowing rock.

77738.e: A volcano blows out a cloud of fine ash, and aeroplanes are not allowed to fly. In 2010, the ash cloud from an Icelandic volcano partly stopped air traffic in Europe for days.
77738.m: An ash cloud can be dangerous for aeroplanes.

77739.q: What kind of island do these emojis make?
77739.e: Volcano and island make volcanic island. Iceland and Hawaii, for example, were formed by volcanoes.
77739.m: Many islands in the sea were formed by volcanoes.

77740.q: Which phenomenon do these pictures show?
77740.e: Hot water that shoots up into the air is a geyser. The water is heated underground by volcanic heat.
77740.m: A geyser shoots hot water out of the ground into the air.

77741.q: Which part of the volcano is meant?
77741.e: The funnel-shaped opening at the top of the volcano is called the crater. Lava, gas and ash come out through it during an eruption.
77741.m: The crater is the opening at the top of a volcano.

77742.q: What is the thing shown here called?
77742.e: Molten rock deep under the volcano is called magma. Only when it reaches the surface is it called lava.
77742.m: Under the ground, molten rock is called magma; at the surface, lava.

77743.q: Which rock do these pictures show?
77743.e: Pumice is a light rock from volcanoes that is full of tiny air holes. It is used, for example, to remove hard skin from your feet.
77743.m: Pumice is so light that it can even float on water.

77744.q: Which substance smells like this at volcanoes?
77744.e: A volcano and the smell of rotten eggs stand for sulphur. Gases containing sulphur pour out of volcanoes and smell strongly.
77744.m: Sulphur gases at volcanoes smell of rotten eggs.

77745.e: Lightning and a loud noise make thunder. The lightning heats the air so much that it suddenly expands with a bang.
77745.m: Thunder happens because lightning suddenly heats the air.

77747.q: What is threatening the coast here?
77747.e: A strong storm pushes seawater against the coast, and the water rises much higher than normal. This is called a storm surge.
77747.m: In a storm surge, the wind pushes the sea against the coast.

77748.q: Which wind do these pictures mean?
77748.e: The föhn is a warm, dry wind that blows down over the Alps. When the föhn blows, the view of the mountains is often especially clear.
77748.m: The föhn is a warm wind blowing down from the Alps.

77750.q: What is lying on the plants here?
77750.e: Morning and water drops on grass make morning dew. On cool nights, water vapour from the air condenses into tiny drops.
77750.m: Morning dew forms when the air cools down at night.

77751.q: Which sight in the sky do these pictures show?
77751.e: A green glow in the night sky in the far north is the northern lights. They appear when particles from the Sun hit the Earth's atmosphere.
77751.m: You see the northern and southern lights mainly near the poles.

77752.q: What is falling from the thundercloud here?
77752.e: Ice balls from a thundercloud that damage fields are hail. In the cloud, the balls are tossed up and down and grow as they go.

77753.q: Which kitchen appliance do these pictures make?
77753.e: Micro (microscope) and wave make microwave. In 1945, Percy Spencer noticed that microwaves melted a chocolate bar in his pocket.
77753.m: The microwave heats food with invisible waves.

77754.e: A pin that is safely closed makes safety pin. The American Walter Hunt patented it in 1849.
77754.m: On a safety pin, the point is safely covered.

77755.q: Which device do these emojis make?
77755.e: Net (web) and camera make webcam. With it you can send pictures live over the internet.
77755.m: With a webcam you can make video calls over the internet.

77756.q: Which device has a name that means what these pictures show?
77756.e: The telescope stands for far, the speaking head for voice. The word telephone comes from Greek: tele means far and phone means voice.
77756.m: With a telephone, people can talk to each other over long distances.

77757.q: Which device in the living room is meant?
77757.e: The telescope stands for far, the eyes for seeing. The word television comes from tele (far) and vision (seeing): a device that shows moving pictures from far away.
77757.m: The television shows pictures that were filmed far away.

77758.q: Which invention do these pictures make?
77758.e: Writing and a machine make typewriter. With it, people typed letters straight onto paper using keys.
77758.m: People used to write letters and texts on a typewriter.

77759.e: Fire heats the air in a large balloon, which then rises. In 1783, the Montgolfier brothers flew the first hot-air balloon with people on board.
77759.m: A hot-air balloon rises because warm air is lighter than cold air.

77760.q: Which writing tool do these pictures make?
77760.e: Ball and writing make ballpoint pen. In its tip, a tiny ball turns and puts the ink on the paper; László Bíró applied for a patent for it in 1938.
77760.m: A small ball turns in the tip of a ballpoint pen.

77761.q: Which invention by Karl Drais do these pictures show?
77761.e: A wooden bike that you push along with your feet is the draisine. Karl Drais presented this running machine in 1817; it is seen as the forerunner of the bicycle.
77761.m: The wooden draisine did not yet have pedals.

77762.q: Which form of energy do these pictures mean?
77762.e: Sun and battery stand for energy from sunlight. Solar cells turn the light of the Sun straight into electricity.
77762.m: Solar cells make electricity from sunlight.

77763.q: Which energy source do these emojis make?
77763.e: Earth and heat make geothermal energy. In Switzerland, many houses are heated with ground probes that take heat from the ground.
77763.m: Geothermal energy uses the heat from inside the Earth.

77764.q: Which plant do these pictures show?
77764.e: The atom symbol and the factory stand for a nuclear power station. Switzerland has (as of 2026) three nuclear power stations, including Beznau and Leibstadt.
77764.m: In a nuclear power station, electricity is made by splitting atomic nuclei.

77765.e: A wall holds back water in the mountains, and this makes a reservoir. The Grande Dixence dam in Valais is about 285 metres high.
77765.m: The water from reservoirs drives turbines in power stations.

77766.e: Black rock is burnt in a plant, and smoke rises. A coal-fired power station makes electricity this way, but gives off a lot of carbon dioxide.
77766.m: Coal-fired power stations harm the climate with lots of carbon dioxide.

77767.q: Which energy makes the lamp light up here?
77767.e: A strong arm, a bike and a lamp show muscle power. When you pedal, a dynamo turns and makes electricity for the light.
77767.m: A bike dynamo turns muscle power into electricity.

77768.e: Wood and fire make firewood. Wood grows back and is therefore a renewable fuel.

77769.e: No more electricity, and you need a candle: that is a power cut. Then the lights, the fridge and the internet stop working.
77769.m: In a power cut, a torch or a candle helps.

77770.q: Which organ controls thinking and movements here?
77770.e: The brain in your head thinks, remembers and controls all movements through the nerves. To do this, it sends electrical signals.
77770.m: The brain controls the whole body.

77771.q: Which word about the body do these pictures make?
77771.e: Heart and drumbeat make heartbeat. At rest, an adult's heart beats about 60 to 100 times a minute.
77771.m: The heart beats without a break for a whole lifetime.

77773.q: Which tooth do these pictures mean?
77773.e: Milk and tooth make milk tooth. Children have 20 milk teeth, which are later replaced by permanent teeth.
77773.m: Milk teeth fall out and make room for the permanent teeth.

77774.e: Blood flowing in a circle makes blood circulation. The heart pumps the blood through the blood vessels to all parts of the body and back again.
77774.m: The heart drives the blood circulation.

77775.q: Which part of the skeleton do these emojis make?
77775.e: A vertebra and a column make spinal column. It is made of many single vertebrae and holds the body upright.
77775.m: The spine carries the body and protects the spinal cord.

77776.q: Which injury do these pictures show?
77776.e: A bone and something broken make broken bone. A broken bone is often kept still with a plaster cast.
77776.m: A broken bone heals when it is kept still.

77777.e: An injection that protects against germs stands for a vaccination. It trains the body's defence system.
77777.m: A vaccination trains the immune system.

77778.q: Which process in plants do these pictures show?
77778.e: With sunlight and water, the green leaf makes sugar. This process is called photosynthesis, and it also produces oxygen.
77778.m: In photosynthesis, plants make sugar from light, water and carbon dioxide.

77780.q: What kind of plant do these pictures show?
77780.e: Climbing and plant make climbing plant. Ivy or beans wind their way up walls and poles.
77780.m: Climbing plants grow upwards on walls or poles.

77781.q: Which group of trees do these pictures make?
77781.e: A needle and a tree stand for a conifer, a tree with needles. Spruces, firs and pines belong to this group.
77781.m: Most conifers keep their needles in winter too.

77782.q: What kind of tree do these emojis show?
77782.e: Leaves and a tree stand for a deciduous tree. Beeches, oaks and maples lose their leaves in autumn.
77782.m: Deciduous trees drop their leaves in autumn.

77783.q: How can you tell the age of a tree here?
77783.e: Year and ring make annual rings. A tree forms one ring in its wood each year, so you can count its age on the trunk.
77783.m: You can read the age of a tree from its annual rings.

77784.q: Which plant do these pictures show?
77784.e: A plant that catches flies like a trap is the Venus flytrap. Its leaves snap shut in a flash when an insect touches them.
77784.m: The Venus flytrap catches insects with its leaves.

77785.q: Which plant do these pictures mean?
77785.e: A leaf that stings your hand belongs to the stinging nettle. Its fine stinging hairs break off and release an irritating liquid into the skin.
77785.m: The stinging hairs of the nettle sting the skin.

77786.e: Rain, trees and a parrot make the rainforest. More kinds of animals and plants live there than in almost any other habitat.
77786.m: A huge variety of animals and plants lives in the rainforest.

77787.q: Which animal do these emojis make?
77787.e: Desert and fox make desert fox, also called the fennec. It gives off heat through its large ears.
77787.m: The desert fox cools itself with its large ears.

77788.q: Which animal of Antarctica is meant?
77788.e: The crown stands for emperor, plus the penguin: emperor penguin. It is the largest kind of penguin and breeds in the icy winter of Antarctica.
77788.m: The emperor penguin is the largest kind of penguin.

77790.q: Which animal of the savannah is meant?
77790.e: Nose and horn make rhinoceros: the name comes from Greek words for nose and horn. The horn really does sit on its nose.
77790.m: The rhinoceros carries its horn on its nose.

77791.q: Which sea animal do these emojis make?
77791.e: Sea and lion make sea lion. Sea lions have small ears and can prop themselves up on their front flippers on land.
77791.m: The sea lion is a skilful swimmer.

77792.q: Which animal do these pictures mean?
77792.e: Ant and bear make ant bear, another name for the anteater. It lives in South and Central America and catches ants and termites with its long, sticky tongue.
77792.m: The anteater catches insects with its long tongue.

77793.q: Which habitat do these pictures show?
77793.e: Far down in the dark ocean lies the deep sea. No sunlight reaches it, and some fish make their own light.
77793.m: It is dark and cold in the deep sea.

77794.q: Which habitat do these emojis show?
77794.e: A dark hole in the mountain with bats is a cave. It is dark and cool there, and bats hang upside down from the ceiling during the day.
77794.m: Many bats sleep in caves during the day.

77795.q: What is forming on the metal here?
77795.e: A bike that is often left out in the rain gets brown patches: rust. Iron rusts when it reacts with water and oxygen from the air.
77795.m: Iron rusts when it gets wet and is left in the air.

77796.q: Which chemical process do these pictures show?
77796.e: A burning candle with smoke shows combustion. A substance reacts with oxygen, and heat and light are produced.

77797.q: Which substance do these emojis make?
77797.e: Lemon and laboratory make citric acid. It makes lemons sour and also helps against limescale in the home.
77797.m: Citric acid is an acid that helps against limescale.

77798.e: Clothes going round and a bottle stand for washing powder. It removes dirt and grease from clothes.
77798.m: Washing powder removes dirt from the laundry.

77799.q: Which term do these pictures mean?
77799.e: Water turns into ice at 0 degrees Celsius. This temperature is called the freezing point of water.

77800.q: Which term about water is meant?
77800.e: At sea level, water boils at 100 degrees Celsius. This temperature is called the boiling point; on high mountains it is lower.
77800.m: At sea level, water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.

77801.q: Which substance do these pictures make?
