78922.e: In autumn the spotted nutcracker hides lots of pine nuts in the ground. Young trees grow from the stores it forgets.
78922.m: The spotted nutcracker plants Swiss stone pines.

78923.q: How old can a Swiss stone pine get?
78923.e: The Swiss stone pine grows slowly and can live a very long time. Some trees are several hundred to about 1000 years old.
78923.m: Swiss stone pines can get very old.

78924.q: What is the wood of the Swiss stone pine especially known for?
78924.e: Swiss stone pine wood smells nice and keeps its scent for a long time. People even fill pillows with its shavings.
78924.m: Swiss stone pine wood smells lovely.

78925.q: What can the Swiss stone pine cope with especially well?
78925.e: The Swiss stone pine grows where winters are very long and cold. It copes well with severe cold.
78925.m: The Swiss stone pine can stand severe cold.

a: a room panelled with Swiss stone pine
78926.e: In an Arvenstube the walls and ceiling are covered with Swiss stone pine wood. Rooms like this are common in houses in the Grisons.
78926.m: An Arvenstube is panelled with Swiss stone pine wood.

78927.q: What is another name for the Swiss stone pine?
78927.e: The Swiss stone pine is also called the arolla pine. In Switzerland people mostly call it “Arve”.
78927.m: The Swiss stone pine is also called the arolla pine.

79028.q: Which organ in your head do you think with?
79028.e: The brain is in the head. We use it to think, learn and remember.

79029.q: How many eyes does a person have?
79029.e: A person has two eyes. With two eyes you can judge well how far away something is.

79030.q: What is the front part of the head with the eyes, nose and mouth called?
79030.e: The eyes, nose and mouth are at the front of the head. This part is called the face.
79030.m: The eyes, nose and mouth are part of the face.

79031.q: Where on the body are the ears?
a: On the sides of the head
At the front of the neck
At the back of the neck
79031.e: The ears sit on the left and right of the head. That way we can hear which direction a sound comes from.
79031.m: The ears sit on the sides of the head.

79032.q: What grows on top of most people's heads?
79032.e: Hair grows on the head. It protects a little against sun and cold.

79033.q: What is the back of the neck called?
79033.e: At the back of the neck is the nape. Strong muscles there hold up the head.
79033.m: The back of the neck is called the nape.

79034.q: What do you wear round your neck in winter against the cold?
79034.e: A scarf keeps your neck warm. You wrap it round once or twice.
79034.m: A scarf keeps your neck warm.

79035.q: Which organ in your neck do you need for speaking and singing?
79035.e: The vocal cords sit in the voice box. When air flows past them, they vibrate and make sounds.
79035.m: The voice box makes our voice.

79036.q: Which piece of jewellery do you wear round your neck?
79036.e: You put a necklace round your neck. Often a small pendant hangs from it.
79036.m: You wear a necklace round your neck.

a: Between the neck and the arm
Between the knee and the foot
Between the hand and the finger
Between the tummy and the leg
79037.e: The shoulder is at the top side of the trunk. That is where the arm begins.
79037.m: The shoulder is between the neck and the arm.

79038.q: What is the flat bone at the back of the shoulder called?
79038.e: The shoulder blade is a flat, triangular bone. It is at the back of the upper back.
79038.m: The shoulder blade is at the back of the shoulder.

79039.q: Which joint can you move furthest in a circle?
79039.e: The shoulder joint is the most movable joint in the body. That is why you can swing your arm in a big circle.
79039.m: The shoulder is our most movable joint.

79040.q: What do you often show when you shrug your shoulders?
a: That you do not know something
79040.e: When you shrug, you lift your shoulders briefly. That way you show without words: I don't know.
79040.m: A shrug often means “I don't know”.

79041.q: Which part of the arm is directly below the shoulder?
79041.e: The upper arm reaches from the shoulder to the elbow. There is a long bone inside it.
79041.m: The upper arm begins below the shoulder.

79042.q: What does it mean to “give someone the cold shoulder”?
a: To give them a friendly hug
79042.e: The saying means that you deliberately ignore someone. You turn away from them, so to speak.
79042.m: If you give someone the cold shoulder, you ignore them.

79043.q: In which sport do players wear big shoulder pads?
79043.e: In ice hockey, players often crash into each other. Shoulder pads under the shirt cushion the knocks.
79043.m: Ice hockey players protect their shoulders with pads.

79044.q: Which joint is in the middle of the arm?
79044.e: The elbow is roughly in the middle of the arm. That is where you can bend the arm.
79044.m: The elbow is in the middle of the arm.

79045.q: What can you do with your elbow?
79045.e: With the elbow joint you bend your arm and straighten it again. That way you can, for example, bring a spoon to your mouth.
79045.m: We bend our arm with the elbow.

79047.q: What was the “ell” used for in the past?
79047.e: The ell used to be a measure of length. It was roughly the length from the elbow to the tip of the middle finger.
79047.m: The ell used to be a measure of length.

79048.q: Where is the “funny bone” that tingles so much when you knock it?
79048.e: At the elbow, a nerve lies just under the skin. If you knock it there, it tingles all the way into your fingers.
79048.m: The funny bone is at the elbow.

79049.q: Roughly how does the elbow move when you bend it?
79049.e: The elbow folds the arm mainly in one direction, like a door on its hinge. In addition, the forearm can twist.
79049.m: The elbow folds like a hinge.

79050.q: What does it mean to “elbow your way” forward?
a: To push ahead without caring about others
79050.e: If you elbow your way forward, you push in front and only think of yourself. It is a saying.
79050.m: If you elbow your way forward, you push ahead without caring about others.

79051.q: Which joint connects the hand to the forearm?
79051.e: The wrist is where the hand begins. It makes the hand movable.
79051.m: The wrist connects the hand and forearm.

79052.q: Where do you usually wear a wristwatch?
79052.e: A wristwatch goes round the wrist. That way you can check the time quickly.
79052.m: You wear a wristwatch on your wrist.

79053.q: How many wrist bones does one hand have?
79053.e: There are eight small wrist bones in the wrist. They are arranged in two rows.

79054.q: Which joint do people especially often injure when they fall onto an outstretched hand?
79054.e: When people fall, they often catch themselves with their hands. This puts a lot of strain on the wrist, and it can break.
79054.m: When you fall onto your hand, the wrist often suffers.

79055.q: Which part of the arm is between the wrist and the elbow?
79055.e: The forearm reaches from the wrist to the elbow. There are two bones inside it.
79055.m: The forearm is between the wrist and the elbow.

79056.q: What do you mainly move when you wave your hand?
79056.e: When you wave, your hand tips back and forth. The wrist makes this movement possible.
79056.m: When you wave, your wrist moves.

79057.q: Which is the largest joint in the human body?
79057.e: The knee joint is the largest human joint. It carries a lot of weight when you walk and jump.
79057.m: The knee is our largest joint.

79058.q: What do you wear on your knees for protection when inline skating?
79058.e: Knee pads have hard shells. They protect your knees if you fall.
79058.m: Knee pads protect your knees when skating.

79059.q: What is the soft area at the back of the knee called?
79059.e: At the back of the knee there is a small hollow. It is called the hollow of the knee.
79059.m: The hollow of the knee is at the back of the knee.

79060.q: How do many babies get about before they can walk?
a: They crawl on their hands and knees
79060.e: Many babies crawl first. They support themselves on their hands and knees.
79060.m: Babies crawl on their hands and knees.

a: At the back of the foot
At the front by the toes
At the top of the knee
At the bottom of the hand
79061.e: The heel is the round back part of the foot. A lot of weight rests on it.
79061.m: The heel is at the back of the foot.

79062.q: What is the largest bone in the foot called?
79062.e: The heel bone is the largest bone of the foot. It forms the heel.
79062.m: The heel bone is the largest foot bone.

79063.q: Which part of the foot usually touches the ground first when you walk normally?
79063.e: When you walk, you usually put your foot down heel first. Then it rolls forwards.
79063.m: When you walk, the heel touches down first.

79064.q: Where do you often get a blister in new, stiff shoes?
79064.e: New shoes often rub at the back of the heel. The rubbing causes a blister.
79064.m: New shoes often rub on the heel.

79065.q: What is the raised part of the shoe under the heel called?
79065.e: The heel of a shoe is the raised back part of the sole. It sits exactly under your heel.
79065.m: The shoe's heel sits under your heel.

79066.q: What does it mean to be “hot on someone's heels”?
79066.e: If you are hot on someone's heels, you follow them very closely. The saying fits, for example, a chase.
79066.m: If you are on someone's heels, you follow them closely.

79067.q: What forms on your heels if you often go barefoot?
79067.e: The skin on the heel gets thicker and harder from pressure. This hard layer is called hard skin.
79067.m: Hard skin forms on your heels.

79068.q: How many toes does a person have altogether on both feet?
79068.e: Each foot has five toes. Together that makes ten toes.

79069.q: What is the thickest toe on the foot called?
79069.e: The big toe is the thickest and strongest. When you walk, you push off with it.
79069.m: The big toe is the thickest.

79070.e: Right on the outside of the foot is the little toe. It is easy to stub on table legs.
79070.m: The smallest toe is right on the outside.

79071.q: How is it best to cut toenails?
79071.e: Toenails cut straight across are less likely to grow into the skin. That prevents pain.

79072.q: What do your toes especially help you with?
79072.e: When you stand and walk, your toes press against the ground. That way they help you not to fall over.

79073.q: In which dance do dancers in pointe shoes stand on the tips of their toes?
79073.e: In ballet there is pointe work. The dancers stand on the tips of their toes in special shoes.
79073.m: In ballet you dance on the tips of your toes.

79074.q: How many toes does a chicken usually have on one foot?
79074.e: Most chickens have four toes on each foot. A few breeds have five.
79074.m: A chicken usually has four toes on each foot.

a: At the front in the middle of the tummy
79075.e: The belly button is on the front of the tummy, roughly in the middle. Almost everyone has one.
79075.m: The belly button is on the front of the tummy.

79076.q: What actually is the belly button?
79076.e: The belly button is a scar that everyone gets as a baby. After that it stays for life.
79076.m: The belly button is a scar.

79077.q: What sometimes collects in the belly button?
79077.e: Fine fibres come off clothes. They can collect in the belly button as fluff.
79077.m: Fluff sometimes collects in the belly button.

79078.q: Which of these animals also has a navel?
79078.e: Mammals such as dogs have a navel, often well hidden under their fur. Chickens, frogs and fish hatch from eggs and do not have a navel like this.
79078.m: Mammals such as dogs have a navel too.

79079.q: How is it best to clean your belly button?
a: Gently with water in the shower
79079.e: In the shower you can wash your belly button gently with water and a little soap. Then dry it well.
79079.m: You wash your belly button gently in the shower.

79080.q: What do people mean when they say a place is “the navel of the world”?
a: It is the most important centre
79080.e: The navel is in the middle of the tummy. That is why a particularly important place is also called “the navel of the world”.

79081.q: Which long organ lies in many loops behind the belly button?
79081.e: The gut lies in the tummy in many coils. It digests the food further.
79081.m: The gut lies behind the belly button.

79082.q: Which part of the body is at the front between the belly button and the neck?
79082.e: Above the tummy comes the chest and then the neck. The heart and lungs are in the chest.
79082.m: The chest is above the tummy.

79083.q: What is the chain of bones in the middle of the back called?
79083.e: The spine runs from the head to the pelvis. It keeps the body upright.
79083.m: The spine is in the middle of the back.

79084.q: What is the right way to carry your school bag?
79084.e: With both straps, the weight is spread evenly. That is kind to your back.
79084.m: You carry your school bag on both shoulders.

79085.q: Which of these animals has a spine like us?
79085.e: Fish are vertebrates like us and have a spine. Snails, worms and insects do not have one.

79086.q: Which swimming stroke is swum on your back?
79086.e: In backstroke you lie in the water with your face upwards. You look up at the sky.
79086.m: In backstroke you lie on your back.

79087.q: Which animal carries a hard shell on its back?
79087.e: The tortoise has a firm shell on its back. When there is danger, it pulls in its head and legs.

79088.q: What is good for a healthy back?
79088.e: Exercise strengthens the muscles of the back. Strong muscles support the spine.

a: At the back of the head
79089.e: The forehead is the top part of the face. It reaches from the eyebrows up to the hairline.
79089.m: The forehead is above the eyes.

79090.q: What is between the forehead and the eyes?
79090.e: The eyebrows grow below the forehead. They keep sweat away from the eyes.
79090.m: The eyebrows are below the forehead.

79091.q: What do you often show when you frown?
a: That you are thinking or annoyed
79091.e: When you frown, wrinkles form on your forehead. Often you are thinking hard or are unhappy.

79092.q: Where can you take a temperature with a special thermometer without using the mouth?
79092.e: There are forehead thermometers. You hold them against or in front of the forehead and read off the temperature.
79092.m: You can also take a temperature on the forehead.

79093.q: What do you wear round your forehead during sport so that no sweat runs into your eyes?
79093.e: A headband soaks up sweat. That way you can see clearly during sport.
79093.m: A headband keeps sweat away from your eyes.

79094.q: What is the bone under the forehead called?
79094.e: The skull is made of several bones. At the top front is the frontal bone.
79094.m: The frontal bone is under the forehead.

79095.q: What does the German saying “jemandem die Stirn bieten” (literally ‘to offer someone your forehead’) mean?
a: To stand up to them bravely
To agree with them straight away
To greet them in a friendly way
79095.e: If you “offer someone your forehead”, you face up to them bravely. You do not simply give in.
79095.m: This German saying means to stand up to someone bravely.

79096.q: Which mythical animal has a horn in the middle of its forehead?
79096.e: The unicorn is a mythical creature from legends. It looks like a horse with a horn on its forehead.
79096.m: The unicorn has a horn on its forehead.

79097.q: What do people often put on the forehead to cool it when someone has a fever?
79097.e: A damp, cool flannel on the forehead feels nice when you have a fever. It cools the skin a little.
79097.m: With a fever, a cool flannel on the forehead feels good.

a: At the bottom of the face under the mouth
79098.e: The chin is the lowest part of the face. It is directly below the mouth.
79098.m: The chin is below the mouth.

79099.q: What does Samichlaus (Swiss St Nicholas) have on his chin and cheeks?
79099.e: In Switzerland, Samichlaus comes on 6 December. He has a long white beard.

79100.q: Which instrument do you hold between your chin and shoulder?
79100.e: When you play the violin, it rests on your shoulder. Your chin holds it in place.
79100.m: You hold the violin in place with your chin.

79101.q: What do we humans have that even chimpanzees lack?
79101.e: Humans are the only living things with a real chin that sticks out. Apes do not have one either.
79101.m: Only humans have a real chin.

79102.q: Where are you looking when you put your chin on your chest?
79102.e: When your chin goes to your chest, your head tips forwards. Then you look down.
79102.m: With your chin on your chest, you look down.

79103.q: What is the area on the side of the head between the eye and the ear called?
79103.e: The temple is on the left and right of the head, next to the eye. The skull is a little thinner there.
79103.m: The temple is between the eye and the ear.

79104.q: Which bird can turn its head especially far round?
79104.e: Owls can turn their head very far, up to three quarters of a full circle. That is because their eyes can hardly move.
79104.m: The owl turns its head very far.

79105.q: What does it mean to “bury your head in the sand”?
a: To refuse to see a problem
79105.e: The saying describes someone who closes their eyes to a problem. They hope it will go away by itself.
79105.m: If you bury your head in the sand, you refuse to see a problem.

79106.q: What do you often have with a cold when swallowing hurts?
79106.e: With a cold, the inside of the throat can be inflamed. Then swallowing hurts.
79106.m: With a cold you often have a sore throat.

79107.q: What does the German saying “Hals über Kopf” (literally ‘neck over head’) mean?
a: In a great rush, without thinking
79107.e: If you do something “neck over head”, you act in a great hurry. You hardly think about it.
79107.m: “Hals über Kopf” means in a great rush.

79108.q: According to an old table rule, what should you not put on the table when eating?
79108.e: A well-known table rule says: elbows do not belong on the table when eating. Your hands may rest on the table.
79108.m: Elbows do not belong on the table when eating.

79109.q: In which animal is a joint on the front leg called the “knee”, although it is really like our wrist?
79109.e: The so-called knee on a horse's front leg matches our wrist. The horse's real knee is much higher up on the back leg.
79109.m: A horse's front “knee” is really a wrist.

79110.q: In which direction can you bend your lower leg at the knee?
79110.e: The knee joint bends the lower leg backwards. Forwards it can only be straightened.
79110.m: The knee bends the leg backwards.

79111.q: Where do children often graze their skin when they fall over in the playground?
79111.e: If you fall forwards, you often land on your knees. The skin easily gets grazed.
79111.m: When you fall over, you often graze your knees.

79112.q: Which part of the leg is above the knee?
79112.e: The thigh is between the hip and the knee. There is a long, strong bone inside it.
79112.m: The thigh is above the knee.

79113.q: What does the German saying “etwas auf die leichte Schulter nehmen” (literally ‘to take something on the light shoulder’) mean?
a: To be able to carry it easily
79113.e: If you take something “on the light shoulder”, you think it is unimportant. Often it turns out to be more important than you thought.
79113.m: This German saying means not taking something seriously.

79114.q: What does it mean to “have someone's back”?
79114.e: If you have someone's back, you help them and stand by them. That makes the other person feel safer.
79114.m: If you have someone's back, you support them.

79115.q: Which wild animal of the Swiss Alps has a beard on its chin when it is male?
79115.e: The male ibex has a short beard under its chin. It also has large, curved horns.
79115.m: The ibex has a beard on its chin.

79116.q: What do many people rest their chin on when they sit thinking at a table?
79116.e: When thinking, many people rest their chin in their hand. That way the head rests comfortably.
79116.m: When thinking, people often rest their chin in their hand.

79117.q: What do many grown men remove from their chin and cheeks with a razor in the morning?
79117.e: In many men, short beard hairs grow every day. If they do not want a beard, they shave them off.

79118.q: Where do many people at the swimming pool wear the key for their locker?
79118.e: The locker key often hangs on a rubber band. You slip it over your wrist and so have the key with you while you swim.
79118.m: At the swimming pool you wear the key on your wrist.

79119.q: What is the part of a shirt that goes round the neck called?
79119.e: The collar is the top edge of the shirt. It goes all the way round the neck.
79119.m: The collar goes round the neck.

79120.q: What are you doing when you “crane your neck”?
79120.e: If you crane your neck, you stretch your head and neck upwards. That way you can see over other people.
79120.m: If you crane your neck, you want to see something.

79121.q: Which bird has only two toes on each foot?
79121.e: The ostrich is the only bird with only two toes on each foot. This helps it run fast.
79121.m: The ostrich has two toes on each foot.

79122.q: What do you sit on in the heel sit position?
79122.e: In the heel sit you kneel and sit with your bottom on your heels. You may know this position from PE.
79122.m: In the heel sit you sit on your heels.

79123.q: Where do koala mothers carry their older young around?
79123.e: When the koala joey is bigger, it clings to its mother's fur. It then rides along on her back.
79123.m: Koala joeys ride on their mother's back.

79124.q: What does it mean to talk about someone “behind their back”?
79124.e: If you talk behind someone's back, you talk about a person who is not there. The other person does not notice.
79124.m: Talking behind someone's back means talking secretly.

79125.q: What does it mean to “rack your brains”?
a: To think hard about something for a long time
79125.e: The saying describes someone who thinks for a long time about a difficult question. Of course, nothing actually gets damaged.
79125.m: If you rack your brains, you think for a long time.

79126.q: How does your chin move when you nod your head to say “yes”?
79126.e: When you nod, you lower and raise your head. Your chin moves up and down.
79126.m: When you nod, your chin moves up and down.

79127.q: What do people often wrap round a sprained wrist?
79127.e: An elastic bandage supports the injured joint. It also helps it to swell less.
79127.m: A sprained wrist is supported with a bandage.

79128.e: Speed tells you how far something travels in a certain time. The more distance in the same time, the faster.
79128.m: Speed tells you how fast something moves.

79129.q: Two children run for the same length of time. Who was faster?
a: The one who covered the longer distance
The one who covered the shorter distance
The one who started running first
79129.e: In the same time, the faster child gets further. So the longer distance is a sign of more speed.
79129.m: In the same time, the faster one gets further.

79130.q: Which bird is the fastest animal in the world when diving?
79130.e: The peregrine falcon dives from high up onto its prey. It reaches over 300 kilometres per hour.
79130.m: The peregrine falcon is the fastest animal when diving.

79131.q: Which bird cannot fly but can run very fast?
79131.e: The ostrich is the fastest runner among birds. It reaches around 70 kilometres per hour.
79131.m: The ostrich is a very fast runner.

79132.q: Which is faster in Switzerland: a tram in town or an InterCity train?
79132.e: InterCity trains travel fast between cities on long, straight stretches. The tram moves slowly through town and stops often.
79132.m: An InterCity train is much faster than a tram.

79133.q: What do the police use to check whether cars are going too fast?
79133.e: A speed camera measures the speed of passing cars using radar. If a car is too fast, it is photographed.
79133.m: The police measure speed with radar.

79134.q: What do you need a stopwatch for?
a: To measure how long something takes
To set the time in the morning
79134.e: With a stopwatch you measure a length of time. You start it at the beginning and stop it at the end.
79134.m: A stopwatch measures how long something takes.

79135.q: Which way does a stopwatch count after you start it?
a: It does not count at all
79135.e: The stopwatch starts at zero and counts the time upwards. A kitchen timer, on the other hand, counts down.
79135.m: A stopwatch counts up from zero.

79136.q: In a ski race, what measures the time very precisely when the skier crosses the finish?
79136.e: At the finish there is an invisible beam of light. When the skier passes through it, the clock stops automatically.
79136.m: A light barrier stops the clock precisely.

79137.q: Which craft is Switzerland famous for all over the world?
79137.e: Watches have been made in Switzerland for centuries, especially in the Jura. Swiss watches are known all over the world.
79137.m: Switzerland is famous for its watches.

79138.q: Nina takes 30 seconds for one lap around the playground. How long does she need for 2 laps if she keeps the same speed?
79138.e: 2 times 30 seconds is 60 seconds. 60 seconds is exactly 1 minute.
79138.m: Two half minutes make one minute.

a: The one who reaches the finish first
The one with the nicest shoes
79139.e: In a race, what counts is who crosses the finish line first. That person was the fastest.
79139.m: Whoever reaches the finish first wins.

79140.q: What is a well-known call to start a race?
a: On your marks, get set, go!
79140.e: Many races start with “On your marks, get set, go!” At “go”, everyone runs at the same time.
79140.m: The race starts at the word “go”.

79141.q: In the fairy tale “The Hare and the Hedgehog”, who waits at the other end of the field?
79141.e: The hedgehog's wife looks exactly like the hedgehog. So every time, the hare thinks the hedgehog is already at the finish.
79141.m: In the fairy tale, the hedgehog tricks the hare with the help of his wife.

79142.q: What is a race called in which the runners pass on a baton?
79142.e: In a relay race, each team member runs one section. Then they hand the baton to the next runner.
79142.m: In a relay race you pass on a baton.

79143.q: What is different about a cheetah's claws compared with a pet cat's?
a: It cannot pull them in completely
It has no claws at all
It only has claws on its back legs
It has twice as many claws
79143.e: A cheetah's claws stay partly out. When it runs, they grip the ground like the spikes of a running shoe.
79143.m: The cheetah cannot fully pull in its claws.

79144.q: Roughly how far does a Roman snail crawl in one minute?
79144.e: A Roman snail manages about 7 centimetres per minute. That is only around 4 metres in an hour.
79144.m: A snail crawls only a few centimetres per minute.

79145.q: What does it mean when someone moves “at a snail's pace”?
79145.e: Snails are very slow. That is why we say “at a snail's pace” when someone dawdles.
79145.m: At a snail's pace means very slowly.

79146.q: What does a snail glide on over the ground?
79146.e: The snail gives off slime and glides on it with its foot. The slime also protects it from drying out.

79147.q: Where are a Roman snail's eyes?
a: At the tips of its long feelers
At the end of its tail
79147.e: The Roman snail has two long feelers at the top. There is an eye at the end of each one.
79147.m: A snail has its eyes on its feelers.

79148.q: What is a Roman snail's shell made of?
79148.e: The snail shell is made of lime. The snail can repair small damage itself.
79148.m: A snail shell is made of lime.

79149.q: What is a snail without a shell called?
79149.e: Slugs have no shell. You often find them in the garden, especially after rain.
79149.m: A snail without a shell is called a slug.

79150.q: A snail has already crawled 10 centimetres and crawls another 5 centimetres. How far has it crawled altogether?
79150.e: You add the two distances together. 10 plus 5 makes 15 centimetres.

79151.e: A ball is round and touches the ground only at one small spot. That is why it rolls easily.

79152.q: What is the easiest way to move a heavy box?
79152.e: Rollers make moving things much easier than dragging. That is why suitcases and shopping trolleys have wheels.
79152.m: Loads are easier to move on rollers.

79153.q: Which invention lets carts and bikes roll?
79153.e: The wheel is one of the most important inventions. Without wheels you would have to drag loads or pull them on runners.

79154.q: What keeps getting bigger when you roll it through wet snow?
79154.e: As it rolls, wet snow sticks to the ball. So it gets bigger and bigger, for example for a snowman.
79154.m: A snowball grows as it rolls.

79155.q: How do you have to put a round tin down so that it can roll?
79155.e: If the tin stands on its flat bottom, it stays still. If it lies on its curved side, it can roll.
79155.m: A tin rolls on its curved side.

79156.q: What do you glide on with ice skates?
79156.e: Ice skates have narrow metal blades. They glide very well on smooth ice.
79156.m: With ice skates you glide on ice.

79157.q: Which animal glides from tree to tree with a spread-out flap of skin?
79157.e: The flying squirrel has skin between its front and back legs. With it, it glides through the air like with a parachute.
79157.m: The flying squirrel glides from tree to tree.

79158.q: What is an aeroplane without an engine that glides through the air called?
79158.e: A glider has long wings and no engine. It glides through the air and uses rising air to climb higher again.
79158.m: A glider flies without an engine.

79159.q: Why do you slide so fast on a water slide at the swimming pool?
a: The water makes the slide slippery
The slide is made of wood
79159.e: The water acts like a smooth film between your body and the slide. So you glide along with hardly any braking.

79160.q: What does a spinning top do when you give it a strong twist?
79160.e: A spinning top stands on a small point while it spins. As long as it spins fast, it does not fall over.
79160.m: A top spins on its point.

79161.q: Why does a spinning top fall over in the end?
79161.e: A fast-spinning top stays upright. As it slows down, it starts to wobble and finally tips over.
79161.m: A top falls over when it gets too slow.

79162.q: What is a spinning top that hums while it spins called?
79162.e: A humming top has holes that air flows through as it spins. This makes a humming sound.
79162.m: A humming top hums as it spins.

79163.q: How do you spin a small table top?
a: With your fingers on the stem
79163.e: You hold the stem between your thumb and index finger. Then you twist it quickly and let go.
79163.m: You spin a table top with your fingers.

79164.q: What does a figure skater do in a pirouette to spin faster?
a: She pulls her arms in close to her body
She stretches her arms out wide
79164.e: When she pulls her arms in to her body, she spins faster. When she stretches her arms out, she slows down.
79164.m: With your arms pulled in, you spin faster.

79165.q: What rolls along a marble run?
79165.e: Marbles are small balls. They roll down the run from top to bottom.
79165.m: Marbles roll along a marble run.

79166.q: How must the run be built so that a marble rolls by itself?
79166.e: On a sloping run, gravity pulls the marble down. On a flat run, it stays where it is.
79166.m: A marble rolls downhill by itself.

79167.q: What can you use to build your own marble run very easily?
79167.e: You can cut open cardboard tubes from kitchen rolls and stick them on a wall at an angle. That makes a marble run.
79167.m: You can build a marble run from cardboard tubes.

79168.q: What does a marble run need on the bends so that fast marbles do not fly out?
79168.e: On a bend, the marble pushes outwards. High edges keep it on the run.
79168.m: On bends the run needs high edges.

79169.q: What happens to a marble that rolls onto a flat carpet at the end of the run?
79169.e: The carpet slows the marble down. Without a slope, it gradually loses speed and stops.
79169.m: Without a slope, a marble stops sooner or later.

79170.q: What do you brake with on most bikes?
79170.e: There are two brake levers on the handlebars. When you pull them, the brakes press against the wheel.
79170.m: You pull bike brakes on the handlebars.

79171.q: When does a bike need a longer distance to stop?
79171.e: When it is wet, tyres and brakes grip less well. That is why you have to brake earlier.
79171.m: When it is wet, the braking distance is longer.

79172.q: What lights up at the back of a car when it brakes?
79172.e: When a car brakes, red lights come on at the back. Then the cars behind know that they must brake too.
79172.m: When braking, red lights come on at the back.

79173.q: Where is the brake on many inline skates?
a: At the back of the boot by the heel
At the front by the toes
79173.e: Many inline skates have a rubber brake pad at the back. You lift your toes and press it onto the ground.
79173.m: The brake pad of inline skates is at the back.

79174.q: What is it called when beginner skiers point their ski tips together and the ends apart to brake?
79174.e: In the snowplough, the skis form a triangle. The angled edges brake in the snow.
79174.m: Beginner skiers brake with the snowplough.

79175.q: What happens to the brakes when you brake for a long time, for example going downhill?
79175.e: When you brake, parts rub against each other. Friction creates heat.

79176.q: What does the speedometer in a car show?
a: How fast the car is going
How much petrol is in the tank
79176.e: The speedometer shows the speed of the car. So the driver knows whether she is going too fast.

79177.q: Where is the speedometer usually found in a car?
79177.e: The speedometer is on the dashboard behind the steering wheel. There it is easy to read while driving.
79177.m: The speedometer is behind the steering wheel.

79178.q: What is the short word for speedometer?
79178.e: In everyday life most people simply say “speedo”. It is the short form of speedometer.

79179.q: What happens to the reading on the speedometer when the car goes faster?
79179.e: The speedometer follows the speed. When the car goes faster, the needle or the number shows a higher value.
79179.m: The faster the car goes, the bigger the number on the speedometer.

79180.q: Where do you usually fix a bike computer?
79180.e: On the handlebars you can see the bike computer well while riding. A small sensor on the wheel tells it how fast the wheel is turning.
79180.m: You fix a bike computer on the handlebars.

79181.q: A car's speedometer shows 50. How fast is the car going?
79181.e: The speedometer shows the speed in kilometres per hour. So the number 50 means 50 kilometres per hour.
79181.m: The number on the speedometer is the speed.

79182.q: What does the speedometer show when the car is standing still?
79182.e: When the car is standing still, it is not moving. That is why the speedometer shows zero.
79182.m: A car that is standing still has a speed of zero.

79183.q: Which device in a car shows how many kilometres the car has travelled altogether?
79183.e: The odometer counts every kilometre driven. It is often right next to the speedometer.
79183.m: The odometer counts the kilometres driven.

79184.q: What is the normal speed limit for cars in built-up areas in Switzerland?
79184.e: In villages and towns in Switzerland, the basic limit is 50. Where there are signs, it can also be lower.
79184.m: In built-up areas in Switzerland the limit is usually 50.

79185.q: What is the normal speed limit for cars outside built-up areas on ordinary roads in Switzerland?
79185.e: Outside towns and villages in Switzerland, the basic limit is 80. Other limits apply on expressways and motorways.
79185.m: Outside built-up areas in Switzerland the limit is usually 80.

79186.q: Which number is on the sign of a 30 km/h zone?
79186.e: In a 30 km/h zone you may drive at most 30 kilometres per hour. There are often such zones in residential areas.
79186.m: In a 30 zone you drive at thirty at most.

79187.q: What does 60 kilometres per hour mean?
a: In one hour you travel 60 kilometres
In one minute you travel 60 kilometres
In one hour you travel 6 kilometres
79187.e: Kilometres per hour tells you how many kilometres you cover in one hour. At 60, that means 60 kilometres in one hour.
79187.m: Kilometres per hour tells you how far you get in one hour.

79188.q: A train travels at 100 km/h for 2 hours. How far does it get?
79188.e: In each hour the train travels 100 kilometres. 2 times 100 makes 200 kilometres.
79188.m: Two hours at a hundred make two hundred kilometres.

79189.q: Roughly how fast does a person walk?
79189.e: When walking normally, an adult covers about 4 to 5 kilometres in an hour.
79189.m: On foot you go about five kilometres per hour.

79190.q: How do you abbreviate “kilometres per hour”?
79190.e: “km” stands for kilometres, “h” for hour. The slash means “per”.
79190.m: Kilometres per hour is abbreviated km/h.

79191.q: Up to what speed does the motor help on a slow e-bike in Switzerland?
79191.e: On slow e-bikes, the motor only assists up to 25 kilometres per hour. If you go faster, you have to pedal on your own.
79191.m: On a slow e-bike the motor helps up to twenty-five.

79192.q: Which is faster: an aeroplane in the air or a car on the road?
79192.e: A large passenger plane flies much faster than any car on the road. That is why you can get to faraway countries quickly by plane.
79192.m: An aeroplane is faster than a car.

79193.q: What is it called when something keeps getting faster?
79193.e: When you accelerate, you get faster from second to second. A car accelerates, for example, when the traffic light turns green.
79193.m: When you accelerate, you get faster.

79194.q: Which other word is often used in everyday life for speed?
79194.e: Instead of speed, people often say pace. For example: the runner set off at a fast pace.
79194.m: Pace is another word for speed.

79195.q: How precisely is the time measured in a ski race?
79195.e: In ski races, the skiers are often very close together. That is why the time is measured to a hundredth of a second.
79195.m: In ski races, hundredths of a second count.

79196.q: What do you use to set a stopwatch back to zero after measuring?
79196.e: A stopwatch usually has a button for resetting. It makes the display jump back to zero.
79196.m: The reset button sets the stopwatch to zero.

79197.q: What marks the end of the course in a race?
79197.e: At the end of the race course there is a finish line. Whoever crosses it first has won.
79197.m: At the end of the course is the finish line.

79198.q: What is a race called in which you have to jump over small obstacles like little fences?
79198.e: In a hurdles race there are hurdles on the track. The runners jump over them during the race.
79198.m: In hurdles you jump over hurdles.

79199.q: In which race do children hop in a sack to see who is fastest?
79199.e: In a sack race you step into a sack with both legs. Then you hop like that to the finish.
79199.m: In a sack race you hop in a sack.

79200.q: What do you carry in an egg and spoon race?
a: An egg in your trouser pocket
79200.e: In an egg and spoon race you run with a spoon with an egg on it. If it falls off, you have to pick it up again.
79200.m: In an egg and spoon race you carry an egg on a spoon.

a: Someone starts running before the starting signal
79201.e: Anyone who starts running too early makes a false start. Then the race is started again.
79201.m: If you start running too early, it is a false start.

79202.q: What is a cheetah's body like?
79202.e: The cheetah is slim and light. With its long legs it takes huge strides when it runs.
79202.m: The cheetah is slim and has long legs.

79203.e: The cheetah is a predator. It hunts other animals and eats their meat.

79204.q: What does a cheetah do before it runs at its prey?
a: It climbs onto a rock and jumps
79204.e: The cheetah first creeps up as close as possible. Only then does it start its short, fast sprint.

79205.q: On which continent do most wild cheetahs live?
79205.e: Most wild cheetahs live in the wide grasslands of Africa. There are still a very few in Asia.

79206.q: How many feelers does a Roman snail have?
79206.e: The Roman snail has two long and two short feelers. It uses the short ones to touch and taste.
79206.m: The Roman snail has four feelers.

79207.q: What does a skateboard have underneath so that it moves?
79207.e: Under the board of a skateboard there are four small wheels. It rolls along the ground on them.
79207.m: A skateboard rolls on four wheels.

79208.q: Which beetle rolls a ball of dung along in front of it?
79208.e: The dung beetle shapes dung into a ball. Then it rolls it away with its legs.
79208.m: The dung beetle rolls a ball of dung.

79209.q: What shape must a wheel be so that it rolls evenly?
79209.e: From the centre, a perfectly round wheel is the same distance from the ground everywhere. That is why it rolls smoothly without bumping.
79209.m: A wheel must be perfectly round.

79210.q: Which large seabird glides over the sea for hours, hardly flapping its wings?
79210.e: The albatross has very long, narrow wings. It uses them to ride the wind and glide long distances.
79210.m: The albatross glides over the sea.

79211.q: In ice hockey, what slides across the ice into the goal?
79211.e: The puck is a flat, hard rubber disc. It slides quickly across the smooth ice.
79211.m: In ice hockey the puck slides across the ice.

79212.q: In which sport do you slide heavy stones across the ice towards a target?
79212.e: In curling, you push a heavy granite stone across the ice. It should stop as close as possible to the centre of a target circle.
79212.m: In curling, stones slide across the ice.

79213.q: Why do curling players sweep the ice with brooms in front of the sliding stone?
a: So that it stops at once
79213.e: Sweeping makes the ice smoother for a moment. So the stone slides further and straighter.
79213.m: Sweeping makes the curling stone slide further.

79214.q: How do penguins sometimes move quickly over ice and snow?
79214.e: Penguins can lie on their bellies and push themselves along with their feet. That way they glide faster than when they waddle.
79214.m: Penguins like to slide on their bellies.

79215.q: What happens if you stand a spinning top on the table at an angle without spinning it?
79215.e: Without spinning, the top cannot stay on its small point. It tips over at once.
79215.m: Without spinning, a top falls over.

79216.q: What happens to the colours on a colourful spinning top when it spins very fast?
79216.e: Our eyes are too slow to see the colours one by one as they rush past. That is why they seem to mix into one colour.
79216.m: On a fast top, the colours mix.

79217.q: What material are many old toy spinning tops made of?
79217.e: In the past, tops were often turned from wood. There are still many wooden tops today.
79217.m: Many tops are made of wood.

79218.e: Marbles are small balls. That is why they roll well in every direction.

79219.q: What happens to a marble that has to roll uphill for a bit?
79219.e: Gravity pulls the marble down. So going uphill, it slows the marble down.

79220.q: How do you build a marble run so that the marble takes a long time?
79220.e: Lots of bends make the way longer. So the marble needs more time to reach the bottom.
79220.m: Lots of bends make a marble run longer.

79221.q: 3 red and 4 blue marbles are rolling on the marble run. How many marbles are there altogether?
79221.e: You add the red and the blue ones together. 3 plus 4 makes 7.
79221.m: Three and four marbles make seven marbles.

79222.q: How do you brake on a bike with a coaster brake?
a: You pull the lever on the handlebars
You press your feet on the ground
79222.e: With a coaster brake, you briefly push the pedals backwards. Then the back wheel brakes.
79222.m: With a coaster brake you pedal backwards.

79223.q: What does the driver use to brake in a car?
a: Her foot on the brake pedal
79223.e: In a car there are pedals at the bottom for your feet. When you press the brake pedal, the car slows down.
79223.m: In a car you brake with your foot.

79224.q: A bike is going at 20 km/h and a car at 60 km/h. How much faster is the car?
79224.e: You calculate 60 minus 20. So the car is 40 kilometres per hour faster.
79224.m: You find the difference by subtracting.

79318.q: Why are pebbles from a stream usually round and smooth?
a: The water has rolled them for a long time
79318.e: The water rolls the stones back and forth in the stream for a long time. This wears the corners away, and the stones become round and smooth.
79318.m: Pebbles are worn round by the water.

79319.q: Where can you find lots of pebbles?
a: On the bank of a river
79319.e: Rivers and streams carry stones along and leave them on the bank. That is why there are lots of pebbles there.
79319.m: There are lots of pebbles on a riverbank.

79320.q: What do you call throwing flat stones across a lake so that they bounce several times?
79320.e: If you throw a flat pebble low across the water, it bounces several times. Some people also call it skipping stones.
79320.m: A flat pebble can bounce across the water.

79321.q: Which shape is best for making a stone bounce across the water?
79321.e: A flat, round stone glides well over the surface of the water. That is why it bounces more often than a ball-shaped stone.
79321.m: Flat, round stones bounce best across the water.

79322.q: Where do the pebbles in Swiss rivers originally come from?
79322.e: In the mountains, stones break off rocks. Streams and rivers carry them down the valley, and on the way they become round.
79322.m: Many pebbles originally come from the mountains.

79323.q: What do you call lots of small pebbles together, for example on a garden path?
79323.e: Gravel is made of lots of small, roundish stones. It is used for paths, squares and in building.
79323.m: Gravel is made of lots of small stones.

79324.q: What is the rock on the Rigi called, in which lots of round pebbles are baked together?
79324.e: Nagelfluh is made of many round pebbles that are firmly cemented together. You can find it on the Rigi and the Rossberg, for example.
79324.m: Nagelfluh is full of round pebbles.

79325.q: Why do pebbles often look shinier when they are wet?
a: The water makes the colours glow
Wet stones are made of glass
79325.e: A thin layer of water makes the surface smooth. This lets you see the colours and patterns of the stones better.
79325.m: Wet pebbles show their colours better.

79326.q: What does granite usually look like?
79326.e: Granite is made of many small grains in different colours. That is why it looks speckled.

79327.q: Is granite a hard or a soft stone?
a: A stone as soft as chalk
79327.e: Granite is very hard and tough. That is why it is used for stairs, fountains and kitchen worktops.
79327.m: Granite is a very hard stone.

a: From hot, liquid rock deep inside the Earth
From sand pressed together on the beach
79328.e: Granite was formed from red-hot, liquid rock. It cooled slowly deep inside the Earth and became hard.
79328.m: Granite formed from liquid rock that cooled down.

79329.q: What often glitters in a piece of granite?
79329.e: Granite contains mica. These are thin flakes that glitter in the light.

79330.q: What is granite often used for?
79330.e: Granite is hard and hardly wears away. That is why streets and squares are paved with it.
79330.m: Paving stones are made from granite.

79331.q: In which part of Switzerland is there a lot of granite?
79331.e: In the Alps, for example at the Grimsel and the Gotthard, there is a lot of granite. You can see huge grey rock faces there.
79331.m: There is a lot of granite in the Swiss Alps.

79332.q: What is the most common colour of granite?
79332.e: Many granites are grey with light and dark dots. But there is also reddish granite.

79333.q: What does the German saying “auf Granit beissen” (to bite on granite) mean?
79333.e: Granite is so hard that you cannot bite into it. If you “bite on granite”, you do not get what you want, a bit like hitting a brick wall.
79333.m: If you bite on granite, you get nowhere.

79334.q: What did a lot of limestone form from?
a: From the shells of sea creatures
79334.e: Long ago, many animals with shells lived in the sea. Their shells sank to the seabed and turned into limestone.
79334.m: A lot of limestone formed from the shells of sea creatures.

79335.q: Which mountain range in north-west Switzerland is largely made of limestone?
79335.e: The Jura is a mountain range made of limestone. You often find fossilised shells from an ancient sea in it.
79335.m: The Jura is largely made of limestone.

79336.q: What happens if you drip vinegar onto limestone?
79336.e: Vinegar is an acid. It dissolves limestone, and this makes tiny bubbles that foam.

79337.q: What are caves with spikes of limestone hanging from the ceiling called?
79337.e: Water dissolves limestone and drips from the cave ceiling. It leaves limestone behind, and slowly dripstones grow.
79337.m: Spikes of limestone grow in dripstone caves.

79338.q: What kind of stone is natural chalk?
79338.e: Natural chalk is a soft, white limestone. It is made of tiny shells of sea creatures.
79338.m: Natural chalk is a soft limestone.

79339.e: Limestone is usually light coloured, often grey, whitish or yellowish. That is why limestone cliffs shine brightly in the sun.

79340.q: What is the huge cave in the Muota valley in the canton of Schwyz called?
79340.e: The Hölloch is in the Muota valley in the canton of Schwyz. It is one of the longest caves in the world and lies in limestone.
79340.m: The Hölloch is a huge cave in limestone.

79341.q: Which white coating builds up inside a kettle over time?
79341.e: Tap water contains dissolved lime. When the water boils, it is left behind as a white coating in the kettle.
79341.m: Limescale builds up in a kettle over time.

79342.q: What are the limestone spikes called that grow down from the ceiling of a cave?
79342.e: Stalactites hang down from the ceiling. The dripstones that grow up from the floor are called stalagmites.
79342.m: Stalactites hang from the cave ceiling.

79343.e: Sandstone is made of lots of grains of sand. Over a long time they were pressed and cemented together.
79343.m: Sandstone is made of grains of sand stuck together.

79344.q: Which stone is much of Bern's old town built from?
79344.e: Many houses, the arcades and the Minster in Bern are built of sandstone. Bernese sandstone is greenish grey.
79344.m: Bern's old town is built of sandstone.

79345.q: What happens if you rub your finger hard over old sandstone?
79345.e: Sandstone is not as solid as granite. If you rub it, single grains of sand often come loose.
79345.m: Grains of sand come off sandstone easily.

79346.q: Why did sculptors like working with sandstone?
79346.e: Sandstone is softer than many other stones. That is why it can easily be shaped with a chisel and hammer.

79347.q: Which famous red rock in Australia is made of sandstone?
79347.e: Uluru is a huge rock in the middle of Australia. It is made of sandstone and glows red at sunset.
79347.m: Uluru in Australia is made of sandstone.

79348.q: What wears sandstone down over time so that it crumbles?
79348.e: Rain, frost and wind gradually loosen grains from the sandstone. That is why old sandstone buildings often need repairing.
79348.m: Wind and rain make sandstone crumble.

79349.e: Depending on what is between the grains of sand, sandstone can be yellow, red, brown or grey. Red sandstone contains iron, for example.

79350.q: What did sandstone form from a very long time ago?
a: From sand on beaches, in rivers or deserts
79350.e: Sand settled in thick layers on beaches, in rivers or in deserts. Under pressure it slowly turned into solid stone.
79350.m: Sandstone formed from layers of sand.

79351.q: Which stone did marble form from?
79351.e: Marble forms when limestone deep inside the Earth is strongly heated and squeezed. This changes the stone.

79352.q: What is white marble especially famous for?
79352.e: White marble can be carved finely and has a lovely shine. That is why artists have made famous statues from it.
79352.m: Statues are made from white marble.

79353.q: Which country does the famous Carrara marble come from?
79353.e: Carrara is a town in Italy. White marble has been quarried there for over 2000 years.

79354.q: What stone is Michelangelo's famous statue “David” made of?
79354.e: Michelangelo carved “David” from a large block of white marble. The statue stands in Florence.

79355.q: Which famous building in India is built of white marble?
79355.e: The Taj Mahal in Agra is a tomb covered in white marble. The other buildings are made of red or pink sandstone.
79355.m: The Taj Mahal is made of white marble.

79356.q: Which little toy balls get their name from marble?
79356.e: In the past, these little balls were often made of marble. That is why they are called marbles.
79356.m: Marbles get their name from marble.

79357.e: Polished marble has a very smooth surface. It feels cool even on warm days.
79357.m: Polished marble is smooth and cool.

79358.q: How can you often recognise marble?
a: By its holes like in cheese
79358.e: Many kinds of marble have fine, coloured lines. These lines are called veins.

79359.q: What does a rock crystal look like?
79359.e: A rock crystal is colourless and see-through. It looks like clear glass or ice.
79359.m: A rock crystal is clear like glass.

79360.q: How many sides does a rock crystal have all the way round?
79360.e: A rock crystal is a column with six side faces. At the top it comes to a point.
79360.m: A rock crystal has six sides.

79361.q: What are people called in Switzerland who search the mountains for crystals?
79361.e: In Switzerland, crystal hunters are called Strahler. They climb around the Alps looking for crystals.
79361.m: In Switzerland, crystal hunters are called Strahler.

79362.q: Where in Switzerland can you find rock crystals?
a: In fields on the Central Plateau
79362.e: Rock crystals are found mainly in the Alps. The areas around the Grimsel and the Gotthard are especially well known.
79362.m: Rock crystals are found in the Swiss Alps.

79363.q: What did people long ago think a rock crystal was?
79363.e: In the past, many people believed rock crystal was ice that never melts. The word crystal comes from the Greek word for ice.
79363.m: People used to think rock crystal was everlasting ice.

79364.q: Which mineral family does rock crystal belong to?
79364.e: Rock crystal is a very pure, clear form of quartz. Quartz is one of the most common minerals.

79365.q: What shape is the top end of a rock crystal?
79365.e: A rock crystal grows as a six-sided column. Its top end comes together in a point.
79365.m: A rock crystal has a point.

79366.e: Rock crystals grow in cracks and hollows in the rock. Over a long time, quartz from the water builds up there.
79366.m: Rock crystals grow in hollows in the rock.

79367.q: How long do large rock crystals take to grow?
79367.e: Rock crystals grow very slowly. Large crystals need a great many years.

79368.e: The ruby is a red gemstone. Its name comes from the Latin word for red.

79369.e: The emerald is a bright green gemstone. It is one of the most valuable gemstones.

79370.q: What colour is a sapphire usually?
79370.e: Most sapphires are blue. But there are also sapphires in other colours.

79371.e: The amethyst is a purple gemstone. It is a form of quartz.

79372.e: Gemstones are rare, beautiful and hard. That is why they are very precious.
79372.m: Gemstones are rare and therefore valuable.

79373.q: What do people do to gemstones to make them sparkle?
79373.e: Gemstones are cut into shape. Their many smooth faces make them sparkle in the light.

79374.q: What are gemstones often used for?
79374.e: Gemstones are beautiful and rare. That is why they are often set in rings, necklaces and crowns.
79374.m: Gemstones are often used for jewellery.

79375.q: Which of a queen's treasures is often set with lots of gemstones?
79375.e: The crowns of queens and kings are often decorated with gemstones. They show power and wealth.
79375.m: Crowns are often set with gemstones.

79376.q: Which stone is the hardest in nature?
79376.e: Diamond is the hardest natural material. It can scratch almost every other substance.
79376.m: Diamond is the hardest stone in nature.

79377.q: What is a diamond made of?
79377.e: A diamond is made only of carbon. That is the same substance that coal is mostly made of.
79377.m: A diamond is made of carbon.

79378.q: What is the unit used for the weight of diamonds?
79378.e: The weight of diamonds and gemstones is measured in carats. One carat is 0.2 grams.

79379.q: Apart from jewellery, what are diamonds used for?
79379.e: Because diamonds are so hard, they are put into drills and saws. With them you can even cut hard stone.
79379.m: Diamonds help with cutting and drilling.

79380.q: What colour is a typical diamond?
79380.e: Most diamonds in jewellery are colourless and clear. But there are also rare coloured diamonds.

79381.q: What is a cut diamond in jewellery often called?
79381.e: A diamond with a special round cut is called a brilliant. This makes it sparkle especially strongly.
79381.m: A cut diamond is often called a brilliant.

79382.q: What can happen if you hit a diamond hard with a hammer?
79382.e: A diamond is very hard, but it is also brittle. A hard blow can therefore split or shatter it.
79382.m: A diamond is hard, but it can shatter if hit.

79383.e: Diamond is harder than glass. That is why you can scratch and cut glass with it.

79384.q: What do you use to pan for gold in the sand of a stream?
79384.e: You put sand and water into a flat pan and swirl it. The light bits are washed away and the heavy gold stays behind.
79384.m: You pan for gold with a gold pan.

79385.q: Why does gold stay at the bottom of the pan when panning?
79385.e: Gold is much heavier than sand and gravel. That is why it sinks to the bottom when you swirl the pan.
79385.m: Gold stays behind because it is heavy.

79386.q: What does gold that you find in a stream look like?
79386.e: In a stream you usually only find tiny flakes of gold. Big lumps of gold are very rare.
79386.m: In a stream you usually find tiny flakes of gold.

79387.q: Can you find gold in Swiss streams?
79387.e: In some streams, for example in the Napf area, the water carries tiny grains of gold. You hardly ever find big pieces.
79387.m: There are tiny grains of gold in some Swiss streams.

79388.q: What happens to gold if it lies in water for a long time?
79388.e: Gold does not rust and does not change in water. That is why it still shines even after a long time.

79389.q: What is a lump of gold found in nature called?
79389.e: A natural lump of gold is called a nugget. Bars and coins are made by people.
79389.m: A lump of gold from nature is called a nugget.

79390.q: What gets washed out of the pan when panning for gold?
79390.e: When you swirl the pan, the water washes out the lighter grains of sand and little stones. The heavy gold is left behind.
79390.m: When panning for gold, you wash the sand away.

79391.q: What is the time called when, from 1848, huge numbers of people moved to California to find gold?
79391.e: From 1848, thousands of people travelled to California to find gold. This time is called the Gold Rush.
79391.m: In the Gold Rush, lots of people searched for gold.

79392.e: Sand is made of small grains of rock. They have been worn off bigger stones by wind and water.
79392.m: Sand is made of tiny grains of rock.

79393.q: Which sand is better for building a sandcastle?
79393.e: Wet sand sticks together because the water holds the grains together. Dry sand trickles apart.
79393.m: You build sandcastles with wet sand.

79394.q: What is the largest hot desert on Earth, where there is lots of sand?
79394.e: The Sahara in Africa is the largest hot desert in the world. Part of it is covered with huge sand dunes.
79394.m: The Sahara is the largest hot desert.

79395.e: Sand is heated very strongly until it melts. This makes glass for windows and bottles.

79396.e: In an hourglass, sand trickles from the top to the bottom. When it has all run through, a certain amount of time has passed.

79397.q: What are the hills of sand called that the wind piles up in the desert?
79397.e: The wind blows the sand together into big hills. These hills are called dunes.
79397.m: Hills of sand in the desert are called dunes.

79398.q: What do you get if you mix sand, gravel, cement and water?
79398.e: Sand, gravel, cement and water together make concrete. When it dries it becomes rock hard, and houses and bridges are built with it.
79398.m: Concrete is made from sand, gravel, cement and water.

79399.q: What happens to water that you pour onto sand?
79399.e: There are lots of small gaps between the grains of sand. That is why water flows through sand quickly.
79399.m: Water soaks away quickly in sand.

79400.q: How does wet clay soil feel?
79400.e: Wet clay soil is soft and sticky and can be shaped. That is why it sticks to shoes and hands.
79400.m: Wet clay soil is sticky and soft.

79401.q: What happens to clay soil when it dries?
79401.e: When the water evaporates from the clay soil, it becomes firm and hard. It often cracks as it dries.

79402.q: What is made from clay that is fired in a kiln?
79402.e: Bricks are shaped from clay. They are fired in a hot kiln, which makes them very solid.
79402.m: Bricks are made from fired clay.

79403.q: Which bird builds its nest out of little lumps of mud?
79403.e: Swallows collect damp mud in their beaks. They use it to stick their nests onto house walls or inside barns.
79403.m: Swallows build their nests from mud.

79404.q: What can you shape out of clay?
79404.e: Clay is easy to shape. After firing, it becomes solid pots, bowls and jugs.
79404.m: You can shape pots out of clay.

79405.q: What have people in many countries built houses from, in the past and today?
79405.e: Clay soil can be found almost everywhere and it is cheap. That is why people in many countries build houses out of mud bricks.
79405.m: Many houses around the world are built of clay.

79406.q: Why does a puddle often stay on clay soil after rain?
a: Clay soaks up water straight away
79406.e: Clay has very fine grains that lie close together. That is why water only soaks into it slowly.

79407.q: What colour is clay soil often?
79407.e: Clay soil often contains iron. That is why it is usually brown, yellowish or reddish.
79407.m: Clay soil is usually brown or yellowish.

a: Remains of living things that turned to stone
A stone that has been painted
79408.e: A petrification shows remains or prints of living things from long ago. Over a very long time they turned to stone.
79408.m: A petrification is a living thing that turned to stone.

79409.q: What is another word for a living thing that has turned to stone?
79409.e: Remains of living things that have turned to stone are called fossils. A single piece is called a fossil.
79409.m: A living thing turned to stone is called a fossil.

79410.q: What does a fossil ammonite look like?
a: Like a snail shell with a spiral
79410.e: Ammonites were sea creatures with a spiral shell. Their fossils look like coiled snail shells.
79410.m: An ammonite looks like a spiral shell.

79411.q: How long does it take for a living thing to turn to stone?
79411.e: A fossil forms slowly over many thousands to millions of years. The living thing gets covered by layers of sand or mud.
79411.m: A fossil takes a very, very long time to form.

79412.q: What did dinosaurs leave behind that was found in the canton of Jura?
79412.e: In the canton of Jura there are thousands of fossil dinosaur footprints. They show where the animals walked long ago.
79412.m: There are fossil dinosaur tracks in the Jura.

79413.q: What are scientists who study fossils called?
79413.e: Palaeontologists study fossils. This is how they learn which animals and plants lived long ago. Archaeologists, on the other hand, study traces left by people.

79414.q: In which yellow resin stone do you sometimes find trapped insects?
79414.e: Amber is fossilised tree resin. Sometimes it contains trapped insects that lived millions of years ago.
79414.m: You sometimes find insects in amber.

79415.q: Why do people find fossil shells on Swiss mountains?
a: There used to be sea there
79415.e: A very long time ago there was a sea where Switzerland is today. Later the seabed was folded up into mountains.
79415.m: Where there are mountains today, there used to be sea.

79416.q: What does baking powder do in cake mixture?
a: It makes the mixture rock hard
79416.e: Baking powder forms lots of tiny gas bubbles in the mixture. These make the cake light and tall.
79416.m: Baking powder makes the mixture rise.

79417.q: Which gas is produced when baking powder works in dough?
79417.e: Baking powder releases the gas carbon dioxide. The gas bubbles puff up the dough.
79417.m: Baking powder makes the gas carbon dioxide.

79418.q: What is a sponge cake like if you forget the baking powder?
79418.e: Without baking powder, hardly any gas bubbles form in the mixture. The cake does not rise and stays flat and dense.
79418.m: Without baking powder, the cake stays flat.

79419.q: Where does baking powder work best?
79419.e: Baking powder needs moisture and, above all, heat. In a hot oven it makes the most gas.
79419.m: Baking powder works mainly in a hot oven.

79420.e: Baking powder is a fine white powder. That is why you can hardly see it in the mixture.
79420.m: Baking powder is a white powder.

79421.q: Which substance is the most important part of baking powder?
79421.e: Bicarbonate of soda forms gas bubbles in moist, warm dough. That is why it is the most important part of baking powder.
79421.m: Baking powder is mainly bicarbonate of soda.

79422.q: Why does a cake made with baking powder have lots of little holes inside?
79422.e: During baking, lots of gas bubbles form in the mixture. The cake sets and the holes stay.
79422.m: The holes in a cake come from gas bubbles.

79423.q: Which bake is usually made with baking powder?
79423.e: Cakes such as marble cake rise with baking powder. Pizza and bread are usually made with yeast.
79423.m: Marble cake is made with baking powder.

79424.e: Yeast is made of tiny living fungi. You can only see the single yeast cells under a microscope.
79424.m: Yeast is made of tiny living fungi.

79425.q: What do the yeast fungi in dough like to eat most?
79425.e: Yeast fungi feed on sugar. As they do, they make gas that puffs up the dough.

79426.q: What makes a yeast dough rise?
79426.e: The yeast fungi make lots of gas bubbles in the dough. This gas makes the dough big and airy.
79426.m: Yeast makes the dough rise with gas.

79427.q: Where does a yeast dough rise fastest?
79427.e: Yeast likes it warm. In a warm place the yeast fungi work quickly, in the cold only slowly.
79427.m: Yeast dough rises quickly in the warmth.

79428.q: What happens to yeast when it gets very hot?
79428.e: Yeast is made of living things. In great heat they die, for example in the hot oven during baking.

79429.q: Which Swiss Sunday bake is made with yeast?
79429.e: Zopf, a plaited loaf, is made with yeast. The yeast makes it nice and soft and airy.

79430.q: What do you call the process in which yeast makes gas and a little alcohol?
79430.e: This process is called fermentation. The gas makes the dough rise, and the alcohol evaporates during baking.

79431.q: In what form do you often buy fresh yeast in the shop?
79431.e: Fresh yeast is usually sold as a small cube. Dried yeast comes as a powder in a sachet.
79431.m: Fresh yeast is bought as a cube.

79432.e: Vinegar contains an acid. That is why it tastes sour.

79433.q: What is vinegar often used for in the kitchen?
79433.e: Vinegar gives salad dressing a sour taste. It is usually mixed with oil and spices.
79433.m: Vinegar is used for salad dressing.

79434.e: The acetic acid evaporates easily and stings the nose. That is why vinegar smells sharp and sour.

79435.q: What can you remove from a kettle with vinegar?
79435.e: The acid in vinegar dissolves limescale. That is why diluted vinegar helps against white limescale rings.

79436.q: What is cider vinegar made from?
79436.e: Cider vinegar is made from apple juice or cider. This slowly turns sour.
79436.m: Cider vinegar is made from apples.

79437.q: Which tiny living things turn wine into vinegar?
79437.e: Acetic acid bacteria turn the alcohol in wine into acetic acid. This is how wine vinegar is made.

79438.q: Why are gherkins pickled in vinegar?
a: So they go soft like mush
79438.e: The acid in vinegar stops many germs. So pickled gherkins stay good to eat for a long time.

79439.q: What happens to the shell of a raw egg that lies in vinegar for days?
79439.e: The acid in vinegar attacks the hard shell. After a few days only the thin skin is left, and the egg is soft like a rubber ball.

79440.q: What do you often get after eating something very salty?
79440.e: The body has to balance a lot of salt in food with water. That is why you are often very thirsty after salty food.

79441.q: Where does most of the salt in Switzerland come from?
79441.e: Deep underground in Switzerland there are ancient layers of salt. The salt is dissolved out with water, and then the water is evaporated.

79442.q: In which place in the canton of Vaud can you visit an old salt mine?
79442.e: Salt has been mined in Bex for centuries. Visitors can ride into the mine on a little train.
79442.m: There is a salt mine in Bex.

79443.q: Why do you add a pinch of salt to the water for cooking pasta?
79443.e: The pasta takes up a little salt while cooking. That makes it taste more flavourful.
79443.m: Salt in the cooking water gives pasta flavour.

79444.q: What do grains of salt look like under a magnifying glass?
79444.e: Table salt forms cube-shaped crystals. With a magnifying glass you can see the little cubes well.
79444.m: Grains of salt are little cubes.

79445.q: Why is salt spread on icy roads in winter?
79445.e: Salt makes ice melt even in the cold. This makes roads and pavements less slippery.

79446.q: Which substance is added to table salt in Switzerland to keep the thyroid healthy?
79446.e: The body needs iodine for the thyroid gland. That is why Switzerland has had iodised table salt for over 100 years.

79447.q: What do you knead salt dough for crafts from?
79447.e: Salt dough is kneaded from flour, salt and water. After drying or baking it goes hard, and you can paint it.
79447.m: Salt dough is made from flour, salt and water.

79448.q: Which plant is sugar made from in Switzerland?
79448.e: In Switzerland, sugar beet grows in many fields. Sugar is made from its juice.
79448.m: Swiss sugar comes from sugar beet.

79449.q: In which place in the canton of Bern is there a large Swiss sugar factory?
79449.e: Sugar has been made in Aarberg for over 100 years. A second sugar factory is in Frauenfeld.
79449.m: There is a sugar factory in Aarberg.

79450.q: What happens if you stir a lot of sugar into a small glass of water?
79450.e: Water can only dissolve a certain amount of sugar. Anything extra stays at the bottom as grains.
79450.m: Water cannot dissolve endless amounts of sugar.

79451.q: Which plant is much sugar made from in warm countries?
79451.e: Sugar cane is a tall grass that grows in warm countries. Its stalks are full of sweet juice.
79451.m: In warm countries, sugar is made from sugar cane.

79452.q: Which sugar is as fine as flour?
79452.e: Icing sugar is very finely ground sugar. It is used for dusting or for icing.
79452.m: Icing sugar is as fine as flour.

79453.q: What can lots of sweets cause in your teeth?
79453.e: Bacteria in the mouth turn sugar into acid. This acid can attack the teeth and cause tooth decay.
79453.m: Too much sugar can cause tooth decay.

79454.q: What is sugar pressed into little blocks called?
79454.e: Sugar cubes are made of pressed sugar crystals. This makes them easy to count.

79455.e: Green leaves make sugar with sunlight, water and air. The plant stores it, for example, in fruits or roots.
79455.m: Plants make sugar in their green leaves.

79456.q: What do you get when a machine spins melted sugar into fine threads?
79456.e: The machine melts sugar and spins it through tiny holes. The threads set at once and form a cloud.
79456.m: Candyfloss is made of fine sugar threads.

79457.q: What do you sprinkle on crème brûlée before browning it with a flame?
79457.e: Under the hot flame, the sugar melts and turns brown. This makes a crunchy crust on top.
79457.m: Sugar is sprinkled on crème brûlée.

79458.q: What is melted brown sugar called?
79458.e: When sugar is heated strongly, it melts and turns brown. This is called caramel.
79458.m: Brown, melted sugar is called caramel.

79459.q: What does sugar smell like when it caramelises?
79459.e: When sugar caramelises, new scents are formed. That is why it smells sweet and slightly toasted.

79460.q: What happens if you heat caramel for far too long?
79460.e: Sugar heated for too long burns. Then it turns black and tastes bitter.
79460.m: Caramel that gets too hot burns and turns bitter.

79461.q: Why is liquid caramel in the pan dangerous?
a: It is hotter than boiling water
79461.e: Caramel only forms well above 100 degrees. It sticks to the skin and burns it badly.

79462.q: Which Swiss dessert has a caramel sauce?
79462.e: Caramelköpfli is a pudding with a brown caramel sauce. You turn it out onto a plate.

79463.q: What happens to liquid caramel when it cools down?
79463.e: As it cools, liquid caramel sets and becomes as hard as glass. This is how hard sweets are made.

79464.q: Which fairground treat has a coating of caramel?
79464.e: Caramelised almonds are heated with sugar in a pan. The sugar caramelises and coats the almonds.
79464.m: Caramelised almonds have a caramel coating.

79465.q: Which Swiss sweet is made by boiling sugar and cream until it is light brown?
79465.e: For Rahmtäfeli, sugar is boiled with cream and butter. The sugar caramelises and turns the mixture brown.
79465.m: Rahmtäfeli are made from sugar and cream.

79466.q: Why does a cut apple with lemon juice turn brown more slowly?
a: The juice slows down the browning
79466.e: In the air, the flesh of the fruit turns brown. Lemon juice slows this change down.
79466.m: Lemon juice keeps apples pale for longer.

79467.q: Which vitamin is lemon juice especially rich in?
79467.e: Lemons are rich in vitamin C. The body needs it, for example, to fight off illness.
79467.m: Lemons contain a lot of vitamin C.

79468.q: What happens when you pour lemon juice into milk?
79468.e: The acid in the lemon makes the protein in the milk clump together. White flakes form.

79469.q: What happens to a dark, tarnished copper coin when you rub it with lemon juice and salt?
79469.e: The acid in lemon juice dissolves the dark layer on the coin. The shiny metal underneath appears again.
79469.m: Lemon juice makes dark copper shiny again.

79470.q: Where in a lemon is the strong-smelling oil?
79470.e: The lemon peel contains tiny oil glands. If you grate the peel, it smells strongly of lemon.
79470.m: The scented oil is in the lemon peel.

79471.q: What can you produce with a lemon, a piece of copper and a piece of zinc?
79471.e: The sour juice and the two metals together form a simple battery. It supplies a tiny bit of electricity.
79471.m: You can build a battery with a lemon.

79472.q: Which group of fruits does the lemon belong to?
79472.e: The lemon belongs to the citrus fruits. Oranges and mandarins are citrus fruits too.
79472.m: The lemon is a citrus fruit.

79473.q: What happens when you drip lemon juice onto a piece of limestone?
a: The stone goes soft like wax
79473.e: The acid in lemon juice attacks the limestone. This produces a gas that forms little bubbles.

79474.q: What happens when you pour sherbet powder into water?
79474.e: In water, the substances in the sherbet powder react with each other. This forms lots of gas bubbles.

79475.q: Which two substances in sherbet powder fizz together?
a: Bicarbonate of soda and an acid
79475.e: Sherbet powder contains bicarbonate of soda and an acid. Together with water they make gas.
79475.m: Bicarbonate of soda and acid make sherbet powder fizz.

79476.q: Which acid is often found in sherbet powder?
79476.e: Sherbet powder usually contains citric acid or tartaric acid. It also gives the slightly sour taste.
79476.m: Sherbet powder often contains citric acid.

79477.q: What do you feel when you sprinkle sherbet powder on your tongue?
79477.e: Saliva is moist. That is why the sherbet powder starts to fizz and tingle on your tongue.
79477.m: Sherbet powder tingles on the tongue.

79478.q: Why must sherbet powder be kept dry?
a: Otherwise it fizzes in the tin
79478.e: Moisture starts the reaction. Then the powder is used up before you put it in the glass.

79479.q: What is a pressed tablet that fizzes in water called?
79479.e: An effervescent tablet contains the same substances as sherbet powder. It is just pressed tightly together.

79480.e: Besides bicarbonate of soda and acid, sherbet powder contains sugar. It gives the sweet taste.

79481.q: Where does sherbet powder fizz faster, in warm or in cold water?
79481.e: In warm water, chemical reactions happen faster. That is why sherbet powder fizzes more strongly there and is finished sooner.
79481.m: Sherbet powder fizzes faster in warm water.

79482.e: Lactic acid bacteria eat the milk sugar. As they do, they make acid, and the milk goes sour.

79483.q: Which acid forms in soured milk?
79483.e: The bacteria turn the milk sugar into lactic acid. This acid gets its name from milk (Latin ‘lac’).
79483.m: Lactic acid forms in soured milk.

79484.q: How does milk change when it goes sour?
79484.e: The acid makes the protein in the milk curdle. That is why soured milk gets thicker.

79485.q: Which dairy product is made with the help of lactic acid bacteria?
79485.e: To make yoghurt, lactic acid bacteria are added to warm milk. They make the milk sour and thick.
79485.m: Yoghurt is made with lactic acid bacteria.

79486.q: Where does milk go sour fastest?
79486.e: Bacteria multiply quickly in the warmth. In the fridge they work only slowly.
79486.m: Milk goes sour quickly in the warmth.

79487.q: What does soured milk taste like?
79487.e: Soured milk contains lactic acid. That is why it tastes slightly sour.

79488.q: What do you get when you let soured, thick milk drain?
79488.e: As it drains, the liquid runs away. A thick, white mass is left behind: quark.
79488.m: Quark is made from soured milk.

79489.q: What is the yellowish liquid that separates from soured milk called?
79489.e: When milk curdles, a yellowish liquid separates off. This liquid is called whey.
79489.m: The liquid from curdled milk is called whey.

79490.q: What happens to egg white when it is cooked?
79490.e: Raw egg white is see-through and runny. The heat makes it white and firm.
79490.m: Cooked egg white turns white and firm.

79491.q: About how long do you boil a hard-boiled egg?
79491.e: A medium egg is hard after about 10 minutes in boiling water. A soft-boiled egg needs only about 5 minutes.
79491.m: A hard-boiled egg boils for about 10 minutes.

79492.q: Can you make a boiled egg raw again?
79492.e: When cooked, the egg white changes for ever. This change cannot be undone.
79492.m: A boiled egg never becomes raw again.
